decisions.reason: UN GTR 9 covers pedestrian protection in frontal impacts with motor vehicles. Its aim is to reduce injuries to pedestrians in frontal impacts, and its tests use legform and headform impactors on the bumper and bonnet area at the front of the vehicle. The product is a rear-mounted "Rear lamp" that provides "Rear position signalling", "Braking indication (stop lamp)", "Reversing illumination" and a "Retro-reflector". The regulation does cover M1 vehicles, but it does not regulate parts at the rear of the vehicle or lighting functions. It does not apply to this product.

(i) By degradation or change in: e.g. engine, gear, brake, suspension, active steering, speed limitation devices;

(i) E.g. airbag and safety restraint systems, emergency calling systems;

related to functions in subparagraphs (a) or (b) which might be observed in the direct view of the driver;
(ii) Acoustical disturbances: incorrect operation of e.g. anti-theft alarm, horn.
(d) Functions related to vehicle data bus functionality:
(i) By blocking data transmission on vehicle data bus-systems, which are used to transmit data, required to ensure
the correct functioning of other immunity related functions.

decisions.reason: This is the title and front-matter of UN R13H, which covers vehicle braking. It creates no obligation for a rear lamp module.
This is the heading 'Scope'. It has no obligation of its own, and the scope text it introduces concerns vehicle braking, not lamp components.

Paragraph 1.1 applies R13H to the braking of M1 and N1 vehicles. The product is a rear lamp (position, stop, reversing, retro-reflector), which is a lighting component. It is not a braking system or a vehicle type approved for braking. The M1 category in the spec does not make the lamp subject to a braking approval.

This is an exclusion for vehicles without manual braking controls. It does not concern a lamp.

This defines approval of a vehicle type with regard to braking. The product is a lamp component, not a vehicle braking approval.
This defines 'vehicle type' for braking approval purposes. It creates no obligation for a lamp module.
This is a vehicle-type criterion (maximum mass) for braking approval. It does not apply to a lamp component.

This clause is a vehicle-type criterion in UN R13H (mass distribution among axles). The regulation covers the braking of whole M1/N1 vehicles. The product is a rear lamp module, not a vehicle or braking system.

This defines the control transmission of the braking system. It does not apply to a lamp.
This defines the energy transmission of the braking system. It does not apply to a lamp.

requirements.quote: A RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4.
requirements.reason: The product has a retro-reflector subject to the RI requirement.

decisions.reason: This is the heading for the minimum RI values that apply to the product's retro-reflector. It creates no obligation of its own.
When applying for approval of the retro-reflector, the applicant must specify the axis or axes of reference.

requirements.text: When applying for approval, the applicant must specify one or more axes of reference, or a range, corresponding to illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° in the RI table.
requirements.quote: the applicant shall specify one or more or a range of axis of reference,
requirements.reason: The product's retro-reflector needs an approval application that states its axis of reference.

decisions.reason: This applies if the manufacturer specifies more than one axis of reference or a range for the retro-reflector. Photometric measurements must then be repeated for each axis, or for the extremes of the range. Whether several axes are specified is not stated, so the obligation is conditional.

requirements.text: If the manufacturer specifies more than one axis of reference or a range, the photometric measurements must be repeated for each different axis, or for the extreme axes of the range.
requirements.quote: the photometric measurements shall be repeated making reference each time to a different axis of
requirements.reason: The product's retro-reflector is subject to this photometric procedure if multiple axes are declared.

decisions.reason: The rear lamp includes a retro-reflector. Class IA/IB photometric measurements use a limited illuminating surface, and the manufacturer specifies its perimeter. The spec does not state the class. A rear retro-reflector on an M1 car would be Class IA or IB.

requirements.text: For photometric measurement of a Class IA/IB retro-reflector, only the illuminating surface within a 200 mm diameter circle is considered, limited to 100 cm2. The manufacturer must specify the perimeter of the area used.
requirements.quote: The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the area to be used.
requirements.reason: The retro-reflector in the rear lamp is subject to photometric measurement over a defined illuminating surface.

decisions.reason: This is a heading for the Class IA and IB requirements, which cover the rear retro-reflector. It creates no obligation of its own.
The rear lamp's red retro-reflector must meet the minimum RI values in Table 3, measured per Annex 4 Part 1. The class is assumed to be IA or IB for an M1 rear retro-reflector.

requirements.text: Red Class IA/IB retro-reflectors must have RI values at or above Table 3 (mcd/lx) at the stated divergence and illumination angles, measured per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4.
requirements.quote:
the RI values for red retro-reflectors
must be equal to or greater than those in Table 3
requirements.reason: The product has a retro-reflector in a red rear lamp.

decisions.reason: Table 3 sets the minimum RI values. The Class IA/IB red rows apply to the rear retro-reflector. The IIIA/IIIB and IV rows do not apply to an M1 car.

requirements.text: Red Class IA/IB retro-reflector minimum RI: at 20' divergence, 300 (0°/0°), 200 (±10°/0°), 100 (±5°/±20°) mcd/lx. At 1°30', 5, 2.8, 2.5 mcd/lx. decisions.reason: The clause applies only if a Class IA/IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane below 750 mm above the ground. The spec gives no mounting height or class.

decisions.reason: This is a heading for the colour requirements of the reflected light. The retro-reflector is subject to them. It creates no obligation of its own.
The night-time colour of the retro-reflector must be tested by the method in 4.2.1.

requirements.text: Test the night-time colour of the retro-reflector according to the method in paragraph 4.2.1.
requirements.quote:
The testing of the colour for retro-reflector (night-time colour) shall be carried out according to the
method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
requirements.reason: The product includes a retro-reflector.

decisions.reason: The reflected light colour of the rear retro-reflector must meet the red night-time colour limits in UN R48.

requirements.text: The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected light must be within the UN R48 limits for the night-time colour (red for a rear retro-reflector).
requirements.quote:
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux must be within the limits for the night-time
colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
requirements.reason: The retro-reflector's reflected colour is regulated.

decisions.reason: This clause covers the resistance tests for retro-reflectors and lets the Type Approval Authority authorize omitting some tests. It is largely a procedural permission for the authority and sets no manufacturer obligation beyond the remark on the approval form.
This is a heading for the chronological order of tests for Class IA/IB retro-reflectors. It creates no obligation of its own.
Table 4 sets the test sequence for Class IA/IB retro-reflector samples. The product's retro-reflector would be tested in this order.

requirements.text: Type-approval testing of Class IA/IB retro-reflector samples follows the Table 4 order, starting with a general specifications visual inspection on all samples.
requirements.quote: General specifications: visual inspection
requirements.reason: The product includes a retro-reflector that falls under the Class IA/IB test sequence.

decisions.reason: This is the body of Table 4. It gives the test sequence (heat, colorimetry, photometry, water, fuels, oils, corrosion and others) for Class IA/IB samples.

requirements.text: Class IA/IB retro-reflector samples undergo the Table 4 tests in the stated order: shapes and dimensions inspection, heat, colorimetry, photometry, water, motor fuels, oils, corrosion, rear face, stability in time and weathering, with the stated intermediate colorimetry and photometry checks.
requirements.quote: Heat: 48 h at 65° ± 2°C
requirements.reason: The retro-reflector in the rear lamp is subject to the Class IA/IB test sequence.

This clause covers where the vehicle approval mark is placed, near the vehicle data plate. It concerns the whole vehicle, not the lamp.
This clause only points to Annex 2 for examples of approval mark arrangements. It is informative and vehicle-level.
This is the heading for the requirements section. It creates no obligation itself. The lighting-device requirement under it applies to the rear lamp.

This is the lead-in to the post-impact requirements. It creates no obligation of its own. Its sub-clause 6.1.1 on lighting and signalling devices covers the rear lamp, which is fitted to an M1 vehicle.

After the Annex 3 low-speed impact test, the lighting and signalling devices must still work and stay visible. The rear lamp (position, stop and reversing functions) is a lighting and signalling device on an M1 vehicle. It is therefore covered when it is fitted to the vehicle.

requirements.text: After each Annex 3 impact test, the lighting and signalling devices must continue to operate correctly and remain visible. Adjustment disturbed by the impact may be corrected only by the normal means of adjustment, and bulbs may be replaced only in the event of filament failure.
requirements.quote: The lighting and signalling devices shall continue to operate correctly and to remain visible.
requirements.reason: The rear lamp provides the rear position, stop and reversing signalling functions, so it must keep working and stay visible after the impact test.

decisions.reason: This clause covers the operation of the bonnet, boot lid and doors. It has no link to a lamp component.
This clause covers vehicle fuel and cooling system leaks. It does not apply to a rear lamp.
This clause covers damage to the vehicle exhaust system. It does not apply to a rear lamp.
This clause covers the propulsion, suspension, steering and braking systems after impact. It does not apply to a rear lamp.
This is the heading for vehicle type modification procedures. It is administrative and carries no lamp-specific obligation.

UN R42 covers the low-speed collision behaviour of front and rear protective devices on M1 vehicles. Paragraph 7.1 covers modifications to a vehicle type approved under R42. The product is a rear lamp module, which is a lighting component and not a vehicle or bumper system, so this clause does not apply.
This is an administrative provision on communicating confirmation or refusal of a vehicle-type approval under R42. A rear lamp component is outside R42's scope.
This is a heading for conformity of production of R42 vehicle types. It creates no obligation, and the lamp is outside R42's scope.

This clause requires vehicles bearing an R42 approval mark to conform to the approved type, including features affecting how the structure behaves in impact. The product is a lamp component and not an R42-approved vehicle or protective device.
This clause requires random checks on serially manufactured vehicles bearing the R42 approval mark. It does not apply to a rear lamp component.
This clause concerns conformity checks on R42 vehicles, which are measurements and the paragraph 6 impact checks. It is not applicable to a lamp module.
This is a heading for penalties for non-conformity of production of R42 vehicle approvals. It creates no obligation for the lamp.
This clause covers withdrawal of an R42 vehicle-type approval. It does not apply to a rear lamp component.
This is an administrative procedure for Contracting Parties on notifying withdrawal of an R42 approval. It is not a product obligation for the lamp.
This clause covers notification when production of an R42-approved vehicle is discontinued. It does not apply to a lamp component.
This is an administrative clause on communicating technical service and administration names, plus the Annex 1 communication form for R42 vehicle approval. It places no requirement on a rear lamp.
This is a field of the R42 approval communication form (date of report). It is administrative and not applicable to the lamp.

UN R42 applies to vehicle-level front and rear protective devices (bumpers) in low-speed collisions. This clause is a line of the approval communication form (report number). It does not apply to a rear lamp component.
This is an administrative field of the R42 bumper approval communication form (approval granted/refused). It is vehicle-type paperwork and does not apply to a rear lamp.
This is a field on the R42 vehicle approval form for the position of the approval mark on the vehicle. R42 covers bumpers and protective devices, not lamp components.
This is the 'Place' field of the R42 communication form. It is administrative and tied to bumper approval, so it does not apply to the rear lamp.
This is the 'Date' field of the R42 communication form. It is administrative and tied to bumper approval, so it does not apply to the rear lamp.
This is the 'Signature' field of the R42 communication form. It is administrative and tied to bumper approval, so it does not apply to the rear lamp.
This lists documents annexed to the R42 vehicle-type approval communication (drawings of structure and protective devices). The product is a lamp component and R42 does not cover it.
These are approval mark arrangements for vehicles approved for front and rear protective devices under R42. The rear lamp is not a bumper or a vehicle type under R42, so they do not apply.
This is the heading of the R42 low-speed-impact test procedure, which tests vehicle protective devices. It does not apply to a rear lamp component.
The scope of the low-speed-impact test is to verify a vehicle's protective devices (bumpers). The rear lamp is a lighting component, not a protective device, so it is out of scope.
This is a heading for the installations and measuring instruments of the R42 vehicle impact test. It is not applicable to a lamp component.
This sets testing ground requirements for the R42 vehicle low-speed impact test. No impact test of the lamp is required under R42.

This is a heading for the vehicle state in the R42 low-speed-impact test. R42 covers the behaviour of the front and rear protective devices (bumpers) of M1 vehicles. The product is a rear lamp module, which is a lighting component and not a protective device or a whole vehicle, so this test setup does not apply to it.
This clause says the vehicle must be at rest during the bumper impact test. It is a vehicle-level test condition. It does not apply to a rear lamp component.
This clause sets the front wheel position for the vehicle impact test. It is a vehicle-level test condition and does not apply to a rear lamp.
This clause sets tyre pressure for the vehicle impact test. It has no bearing on a rear lamp component.
This clause sets the brake and transmission state of the vehicle under test. It is a vehicle test condition and does not apply to a rear lamp.
This clause covers test conditions for vehicles with special suspension or levelling. It is a vehicle test condition and does not apply to a rear lamp module.
This is a heading for the impactor (striker) test equipment. The rear lamp is not test equipment, and it is not a protective device.
This clause specifies how the impactor is built (rigid, hardened steel contour). It is a requirement on the test apparatus and does not apply to the lamp.
This clause specifies the impactor surface geometry. It is a requirement on the test apparatus and does not apply to the lamp.
This clause sets the impactor mass from the vehicle's unladen weight. It is a requirement on the test apparatus and not on a lamp component.
This clause covers impactor orientation. It is a test-setup requirement that does not apply to a lamp.
This clause covers first contact of the impactor with the vehicle's protective device (bumper). The rear lamp is not a protective device, so the clause does not apply to it.

This clause sets the impactor reference height for the vehicle low-speed impact test. UN R42 covers the front and rear protective devices (bumpers) of whole M1 vehicles. The product is a rear lamp module, which is a lighting component and not a protective device. The test apparatus clause does not apply to it.
This clause covers how the impactor is propelled in the whole-vehicle bumper impact test. It is test-rig configuration and does not apply to a rear lamp component.
This heading covers moving-barrier provisions for the vehicle bumper impact test rig. It does not apply to a rear lamp.
This clause covers the carriage and restraining element of the impact test rig. It concerns test equipment for vehicle protective devices and not the lamp.
This heading covers pendulum provisions for the vehicle bumper impact test rig. It does not apply to a rear lamp.
This clause sets the pendulum geometry for the impact test rig. It is test equipment and does not apply to a rear lamp component.
This clause sets the pendulum plane orientation for the impact test rig. It does not apply to a rear lamp component.
This clause sets the pendulum trajectory for the impact test rig. It does not apply to a rear lamp component.
This heading introduces the longitudinal impact test on a whole vehicle's front and rear surfaces. It is a vehicle-level bumper test, not a lamp component requirement.

This clause sets the number of impacts and the vehicle loading conditions for the whole-vehicle bumper test. The product is a lamp component, not a vehicle or protective device, so it is not directly subject to this test.
This clause sets impactor positioning for the vehicle impacts. It is a vehicle-level test procedure that does not apply to a lamp component.
This clause sets impactor placement and reference height for the vehicle impact test. It does not apply to a lamp component.

This clause covers vehicle alignment for the longitudinal impact test on an M1 vehicle's protective devices (bumpers). The product is a rear lamp component, not a vehicle or protective device, so the clause does not apply to it.
This clause sets the impact speed for the vehicle-level longitudinal impact test. A rear lamp module is not tested this way under this clause.
This is a heading for the vehicle corner impact test. It applies to vehicle bumper and protective-device testing, not to a lamp component.
This clause describes which vehicle corners are impacted and at what vehicle weight. It is a vehicle-level test condition and does not apply to a rear lamp component.
This clause covers impactor placement for the vehicle corner impact test. It does not apply to a lamp component.
This clause covers vehicle alignment and impactor angle for the corner impact test. It is a vehicle test setup condition, not a lamp requirement.
This clause sets the corner impact speed for the vehicle test. It does not apply to a rear lamp component.
This is a heading for repair, replacement and measurement conditions in the vehicle low-speed impact test. It creates no obligation for a lamp component.
This clause allows protective devices and their mountings to be repaired or replaced between vehicle impact tests. A rear lamp is not a protective device.
This clause covers recovery time for self-restoring materials in protective devices (bumpers). It does not apply to the rear lamp module.
This clause covers vehicle-use options for the manufacturer in the impact tests. It is a vehicle-level test procedure that does not apply to the lamp component.
This clause lets the same vehicle be used for tests under other Regulations. It is a vehicle test administration provision and does not apply to a lamp component.

Annex 3 / 3.5 deals with vehicle low-speed impact tests run above the stated speed or mass. UN R42 covers whole M1 vehicles and their bumpers and protective devices. The product is a rear lamp component, not a vehicle or a protective device, so the clause does not apply to it.

Annex 3 / 3.6 sets the accuracy of the speed-recording instrument for the vehicle impact test. It is a test-laboratory condition for vehicle-level R42 tests. It does not place any obligation on a rear lamp component.
This is only a heading for equivalent test methods in the R42 vehicle impact test annex. It creates no obligation, and the rear lamp is outside R42's vehicle and bumper scope.
Annex 3 / 4.1 allows equivalent methods for the R42 vehicle low-speed impact test. It applies to vehicle or bumper approval testing, not to a stand-alone rear lamp module.
This is the document title and version banner. It has no scope or obligation that applies to the product.

The scope covers installation of lighting and light-signalling devices on M, N and O vehicles. The rear lamp is for an M1 passenger car, so R48 installation rules apply to it. The scope clause only sets applicability and creates no separate obligation.
This is the Definitions heading. The terms under it apply to the product's lamp functions, but the heading creates no obligation.
This is the General definitions heading. The definitions beneath it apply to the lamp and its functions, but the heading creates no obligation.

R48 definitions apply to the LSD, RID and RRD regulations. The rear lamp combines light-signalling functions and a retro-reflector, so these definitions govern its terminology. The clause is a definitional link and creates no separate obligation.

This clause says references to standard (étalon) light sources point to Regulations 37, 99 and 128. The spec lists only LED modules on a PCB and does not say a standard light source is used. It is a cross-reference rule and creates no obligation for this product.

This defines 'approval of a vehicle' as vehicle-type approval for the number and mode of installation of lighting devices. The product is a lamp module, not a vehicle type, and the clause creates no obligation for it.

A 'device' is an element or assembly performing one or more functions. The rear lamp is one housing combining position, stop and reversing lamps and a retro-reflector, so it fits this definition. The clause is a definition and creates no obligation.

A lighting function illuminates the road in the direction of vehicle movement. The reversing lamp's illumination function falls under this definition. The clause is a definition and creates no obligation.

A light-signalling function is light emitted or reflected to inform other road users. The rear position, stop and reversing lamps and the retro-reflector all fit this definition. The clause is a definition and creates no obligation.

This defines a lamp as a device that illuminates the road or emits a light signal, and it says retro-reflectors are also regarded as lamps. The product's lamps and its retro-reflector therefore count as lamps under R48. The clause is a definition and creates no obligation.

The change index is specific to each lamp function under the LSD, RID and RRD Regulations. It applies to each function of the product (position, stop, reversing, retro-reflector). The clause is a definition and creates no obligation.
This clause defines 'manufacturer logo'. The rear lamp specification mentions no logo, and the definition creates no obligation for this product.
This heading introduces the vehicle-type definitions that govern R48 installation approval for M1 vehicles fitted with this rear lamp. It is background only and creates no obligation.

This definition sets what counts as a vehicle type for lamp installation, including changes in the kind, number and positioning of lamps. The rear lamp is installed on an M1 vehicle, so the definition is background for approval. It creates no direct obligation.
This is a vehicle-level criterion on vehicle dimension and shape. It does not concern the rear lamp module itself.

The number and positioning of devices defines vehicle type for lamp installation. The rear lamp combines position, stop and reversing functions and a retro-reflector, all of which are devices to be counted and positioned. It is a definitional criterion only and creates no obligation.
This clause covers the headlamp-levelling system. A rear lamp has no headlamp or levelling function.
This clause covers the vehicle suspension system, which is unrelated to the rear lamp module.
This is a heading for the vehicle definitions and creates no obligation for the lamp.
This defines the unladen vehicle condition, which is a vehicle-level measurement state. It is not a requirement on the rear lamp module, and no product facts connect to it.
This defines the laden vehicle condition, which is used mainly for headlamp aiming and levelling. It is not relevant to a rear lamp module.
The extreme outer edge definition is the reference for the width positioning of rear position lamps and other rear lamps on an M1 vehicle. It is background only and creates no obligation.
This sub-item lists a projection (tyres and tyre-pressure gauge connections) that is disregarded when finding the vehicle's extreme outer edge. It does not concern the rear lamp.
This clause covers anti-skid devices on wheels when defining the extreme outer edge. It has no connection to a rear lamp module.
This clause covers devices for indirect vision, which are mirrors and similar devices. The rear lamp module is not one.

This definition says rear position lamps and retro-reflectors are disregarded when determining the vehicle's extreme outer edge. The product contains both, so it is relevant background for their installation. It sets no obligation of its own.
This clause covers customs seals and the devices that secure them. It does not apply to a rear lamp.
This clause covers service-door lighting on M2 and M3 vehicles. The product is a rear lamp for an M1 car.
This definition of overall dimensions is background for the lateral positioning limits that R48 sets for rear position lamps and retro-reflectors. It sets no obligation of its own.
Overall width is the reference for the lateral installation limits of the rear position lamp and retro-reflector. This is a definition only, with no standalone obligation.

Overall length concerns the vehicle length and the projections it disregards, such as end-outline marker lamps and coupling devices. The product spec has no length-related function or end-outline marker lamp.
This defines the operating tell-tale, which is a dashboard or vehicle-level indicator. The product is a lamp module with no tell-tale function in the spec.
This defines the closed-circuit tell-tale, which is a vehicle-level indicator. The lamp module itself has no tell-tale in the spec.

Ground is the reference surface for the mounting-height measurements that R48 sets for rear position, stop, reversing and retro-reflector devices. This is a definition only, with no standalone obligation.
This defines movable body components. The spec does not say the lamp is mounted on a movable component such as a tailgate.

This defines the normal position of movable vehicle components. The spec does not say the lamp is mounted on a movable component such as a tailgate. It describes only a lamp module, and the definition sets no obligation on it.
This is a lead-in to the vehicle-level definition of 'normal condition of use'. It sets no obligation on a rear lamp component and is not tied to any product fact.
This is a vehicle-state definition for motor vehicles (ready to move, propulsion running). It creates no obligation on the lamp component, and the spec gives no movable-component facts.
This definition covers trailers. The product is for an M1 passenger car, so it does not apply.
This is a lead-in to the vehicle-level definition of 'park condition'. It sets no obligation on a rear lamp component.
This is a vehicle-state definition (standstill, propulsion off). It creates no obligation on the lamp, and the spec gives no movable-component facts.

This heading introduces the lamp-generality definitions (grouped, combined, reciprocally incorporated, single-function). They describe a multi-function rear lamp in one housing. The heading itself creates no obligation.
This defines equivalent (replacement) lamps authorised in the country of registration. The spec gives no replacement or equivalence context.
This defines independent lamps, which have separate surfaces, sources and bodies. The product combines several functions in a single housing, so it is not an independent lamp.

This defines grouped lamps (separate surfaces and sources, common lamp body). The product has several functions with LED modules in a single housing, so it may be classified as grouped. The clause is a definition and creates no obligation.
This defines combined lamps (common source and common body). It is a possible classification for the multi-function housing. It is a definition only and creates no obligation.

This defines reciprocally incorporated lamps and also contains the single-function lamp definition. Both are relevant to classifying the multi-function rear lamp (position, stop, reversing). It is a definition only and creates no obligation.
This defines a concealable or retractable lamp. The rear lamp spec describes no concealing or retracting mechanism.

This definition sets how the distance between two lamps facing the same direction is measured. It is background for installation spacing of the module's several lamp functions. It creates no obligation by itself.

This defines an optional lamp. The spec doesn't say any of the functions are optional, and rear position, stop and reversing lamps are normally required on M1 vehicles. The definition adds no applicable obligation.
This defines a pair as lamps of the same function on the left and right of the vehicle. Rear lamps on an M1 car are installed as left and right sets. It is a definition with no obligation of its own.
This defines a matched pair that complies with photometric requirements as a pair. The spec gives no indication that the lamps are approved or used as a matched pair.
This is only a heading for the single and multiple lamps definitions. It has no content that could apply to the product.

This defines a single lamp as a device or part of a device with one lighting or signalling function. Each function of the module (position, stop, reversing, retro-reflector) falls under this terminology. It is a definition and creates no obligation.
This covers two lamps in the shape of a band or strip with a single light-emitting surface. The spec doesn't describe a band or strip lamp.
This defines an interdependent lamp system of two or three lamps providing the same function. The spec describes a single multi-function housing, not interdependent lamps.
This defines lamps marked "Y". The spec describes no interdependent lamps with separate lamp bodies.
This defines lamps marked "D". The spec gives no indication that independent lamps are assembled into a single lamp.
This concerns headlamp classes. The product is a rear lamp, not a headlamp.
This is a heading for definitions about headlamps with driving-beam or symmetrical passing-beam for categories L and T. The product is an M1 rear lamp, so it does not apply.
This defines the additional lighting unit for bend lighting in headlamp systems. The product has no headlamp or bend-lighting function.
This heading introduces the definitions for retro-reflectors. The product includes a retro-reflector. The heading is background only and creates no obligation.
This defines retro-reflection, the property of the product's retro-reflector. It is background only and creates no obligation.

This defines the retro-reflective device and its classes, including IB and IIIB for devices combined with other signal lamps. The product's retro-reflector is combined with lamps in one housing. It is a definition only and creates no obligation.
This is a heading for retro-reflective marking material, such as plates and tapes. The product is a rear lamp with an integrated retro-reflector, not marking material.
This defines retro-reflective marking material, which is a surface or device used for conspicuity marking. The product is a lamp module, not marking material.
This defines the rear marking plate for heavy and long vehicles. The product is an M1 rear lamp and is not a marking plate.
This defines the slow moving vehicle rear marking plate. The product is not an SMV plate.
This defines a sample unit within the retro-reflective marking definitions. It concerns approval sampling of marking devices. It imposes no installation obligation on the rear lamp.
This defines fluorescence for marking materials. The spec mentions no fluorescent material in the product.
This defines the driving-beam (main-beam) headlamp. The product is a rear lamp with position, stop and reversing functions and has no driving-beam function.
These are definitions of an auxiliary driving-beam lamp and a passing-beam headlamp. The product is a rear lamp with no front beam functions.
This defines the principal passing-beam, which is a headlamp concept. It does not apply to a rear lamp.
This defines a direction-indicator lamp. The product's listed functions are position, stop, reversing and retro-reflector, and it has no direction indicator.
This defines the stop lamp, which is one of the product's functions. It is a definition only and creates no separate obligation.
This defines a rear-registration plate illuminating device. The product has no licence plate lamp function.
This defines a front position lamp. The product is a rear lamp.
This defines the rear position lamp, which is a product function. It is a definition only and creates no obligation.
This defines the retro-reflector, which is a main part of the product. It is a definition only and creates no obligation.
This is an exclusion for retro-reflecting number plates. The product's retro-reflector is not a number plate.
This is an exclusion for ADR dangerous-goods retro-reflecting signals. It does not describe the product's retro-reflector.
This is an exclusion for national-requirement retro-reflective plates and signals. It does not describe the product's retro-reflector.
This is an exclusion for Class D, E or F retro-reflecting materials used for other purposes. It does not describe the product's retro-reflector.

This defines conspicuity marking, which is retro-reflective side or rear marking such as tape. The product's retro-reflector is a rear retro-reflector built into the lamp housing. It is not a vehicle contour or line marking.
This defines contour marking, a type of conspicuity marking that shows vehicle dimensions. The product is a rear lamp module and has no contour marking.
This defines full contour marking. The product has no vehicle outline marking.
This defines partial contour marking. The product has no vehicle outline marking.
This defines line marking. The product is a rear lamp module and has no line marking.
This defines a front fog lamp. The product is a rear lamp with no front fog function.
This defines a rear fog lamp. The product's listed functions are position, stop, reversing and retro-reflection, and rear fog is not among them.

This defines the reversing lamp, which is one of the product's functions ("Reversing illumination"). It is a definition only, so it sets no obligations of its own. It gives background for the reversing-lamp installation clauses.
This defines the parking lamp and the end-outline marker lamp. The product has neither function. Its rear position lamp is not described as a parking lamp.
This defines a side marker lamp. The product has no side marker function.
This defines a daytime running lamp, which faces forward. The product is a rear lamp.
This defines the cornering lamp and the exterior courtesy lamp. The product has neither function.

This defines the manoeuvring lamp, which gives supplementary side or rear illumination during slow manoeuvres. The spec lists position, stop and reversing lamps and a retro-reflector, with no manoeuvring lamp.
This defines an external status indicator for alarm and immobilizer systems. The rear lamp has no such function.
This defines a reversing projector. The product has a reversing lamp for reversing illumination, and nothing in the spec describes a reversing projection device.
This is only a sub-heading ("Signal") that groups definitions and creates no obligation.
This defines the hazard warning signal, which is the simultaneous operation of all direction-indicator lamps. The rear lamp has no direction indicator function in its spec.
This defines the emergency stop signal. The spec lists only a basic braking indication (stop lamp) and does not describe an emergency stop signal function.
This defines the rear-end collision alert signal (RECAS), which the spec does not mention.
This defines the answer-back signal used to locate a parked vehicle. The spec has no such function.
This is only a sub-heading ("System") that groups definitions and creates no obligation.
This defines aiming of a beam on an aiming screen, which concerns headlamp beams. The rear signalling lamp has no beam aiming function.
This defines adjustment of beam aim. The spec describes no aiming or adjustment system for the rear lamp.
This defines bend lighting, a front lighting function. It does not apply to a rear lamp.

This clause defines the adaptive front lighting system (AFS), which provides dipped and main beams. The product is a rear lamp with position, stop, reversing and retro-reflector functions. It has no front-lighting or AFS function.
This clause defines an AFS lighting unit, which provides front lighting functions. The rear lamp has no front lighting function.
This clause defines an AFS installation unit, which is a housing containing AFS lighting units. The rear lamp housing contains no AFS units.
This clause defines AFS lighting modes for passing beam and main beam. It does not apply to a rear lamp.
This clause defines the AFS system control. The product has no AFS.
This clause defines AFS control signals. The product has no AFS.
This clause defines the AFS neutral state for passing or main beam. It does not apply to a rear lamp.
This clause defines an adaptive main beam, which is a front lighting function. The product is a rear lamp.
This is a heading for AFS definitions. The product has no AFS, and the heading creates no obligation.
This clause defines passing-beam classes C, V, E and W. They are front-lighting concepts and do not apply to a rear lamp.
This clause defines bending modes of front lighting. It does not apply to a rear lamp.
This clause defines right and left side in terms of AFS lighting units. The product has no AFS, so the definition does not apply.
This defines an AFS (adaptive front-lighting system) control signal. The product is a rear lamp with no AFS function.
This defines a signal generator for AFS system tests. It does not apply to a rear lamp.

This is an AFS-section definition of a supply and operating device. The product is a rear lamp, not an AFS, so it falls outside the AFS scope. The lamp's LED modules are not described as having an AFS control gear.
This defines the AFS system reference axis for front lighting units. It does not apply to a rear lamp.
This defines the traffic-change function for front lighting. It does not apply to a rear lamp.
This defines a substitute function for front lighting and front light-signalling. It does not apply to a rear lamp.
This defines a functional unit for AFS light distribution modes and classes. It does not apply to a rear lamp.
This heading introduces the general switching and activation definitions. They are used for the rear lamp's position, stop and reversing functions. The heading creates no obligation of its own.
This general definition of "Switch ON" applies to the rear lamp's illuminating and signalling functions: position, stop and reversing. It is background only and creates no obligation.
This general definition of "Switch OFF" applies to the rear lamp's illuminating and signalling functions. It is background only and creates no obligation.
This general definition of "Activate" applies to the rear lamp's illuminating and signalling functions. It is background only and creates no obligation.
This general definition of "Deactivate" applies to the rear lamp's illuminating and signalling functions. It is background only and creates no obligation.

This defines sequential activation of light sources, which applies to sequential direction indicators. The rear lamp spec lists only position, stop, reversing and retro-reflector functions, and says nothing about sequential switching.
This defines a retro-reflecting optical unit. The product includes a retro-reflector made of molded prism optics. It is a definition only, so it creates no obligation.
Driver Assistance Projection concerns modifying the light distribution, which applies to headlamps. The rear lamp has no such function.
Risk of Collision Time applies to adaptive or driver-assistance lighting. The spec has no such feature.
This defines a basic element of a reversing projection. The product has a reversing lamp, but nothing in the spec indicates it projects patterns on the ground.
A reversing projection is a light signal projected on the ground by reversing projectors. The spec describes only 'reversing illumination' and gives no ground projection function.
This is a heading for the lens definitions. The product has an outer lens. It creates no obligation.
This defines the lens as the outermost light-transmitting component. The product has an outer lens made of red-tinted PMMA. It is a definition only, so it creates no obligation.
This defines a coating applied to the outer face of a lens. The spec mentions only a metallised coating on the reflector surface, not on the lens, and gives no lens coating.
The spec does not state that the outer lens is textured or designed to divert light. The lens is described only as red-tinted, UV-stabilised PMMA.
This is a heading for the light source definitions. The product uses LED light sources. It creates no obligation.
This defines a light source. The product uses LED modules on a PCB as its light sources. It is a definition only, so it creates no obligation.

The definition applies only if the LED light sources can be inserted and removed without tools. The spec only says 'LED modules on PCB' and does not say whether the sources are replaceable. It is a definition and creates no obligation.

The definition applies only if the LED sources can be replaced only by replacing the device or module. The spec does not state this. LEDs on a PCB suggest non-replaceable sources, but that is not confirmed. It is a definition and creates no obligation.
The lamp uses LED modules on a PCB inside a lamp-specific housing. The 'light source module' definition is relevant background for classifying them. It creates no obligation of its own.
The light source is LED. No filament lamps are specified.
The light source is LED. No gas-discharge sources are specified.
The spec lists LED modules as the light source. This definition of an LED light source is relevant background and creates no obligation.
The spec gives no indication of LED substitute light sources, meaning LEDs replacing a filament or other category. The lamp uses integrated LED modules.
The spec lists 'LED modules on PCB' as the light source. This definition of an LED module is relevant background and creates no obligation.
LED modules usually need current or voltage control. The spec does not say whether electronic control gear is present or what form it takes. It is a definition and creates no obligation.
A ballast controls gas-discharge sources. The product uses LEDs.
The spec does not describe any variable intensity control for the rear signalling functions.
This is a heading for the photometry definitions. The product's light functions and retro-reflector fall under these photometry-related definitions. It creates no obligation.
Definition. The rear lamp uses LED modules on a PCB, so 'objective luminous flux' for an LED module applies as background. It creates no obligation of its own.
Definition. The rear lamp has an outer lens and a retro-reflector, and the light emitting surface must be declared on the drawing. It is background with no standalone obligation.
Heading for the illuminating surface definitions, which apply to the lamp's functions. No obligation.
Definition. It covers the illuminating surface of lighting devices, including the reversing lamp (2.5.12), which is one of the product's functions. No obligation.

Definition. It covers the illuminating surface of the rear position and stop lamp functions, which are light-signalling devices other than retro-reflectors. It is used to verify position and visibility. No obligation.
Definition. The product includes a retro-reflector, and this defines its illuminating surface. No obligation.
Definition. The apparent surface is used for visibility and geometric visibility assessment of the lamp functions. No obligation.
Definition. The reference axis is set by the lamp manufacturer and is used for photometry and installation of the rear lamp. No obligation.
Definition. The centre of reference is specified by the lamp manufacturer for the lamp functions and the retro-reflector. No obligation.
Definition. Angles of geometric visibility apply to the rear position, stop and reversing functions and to the retro-reflector. No obligation.
Definition. Photometric stability applies to photometric measurement of the LED lamp functions. No obligation.
Definition of the goniophotometer system used for photometric measurements of the lamp. It is background only and creates no obligation.

2.5.12. "Reversing lamp" means the lamp used to illuminate the road to the rear of the vehicle and to warn other

be inserted within the bodywork.

decisions.reason: This heading introduces the geometric visibility provisions. Those provisions apply to the rear position, stop and reversing lamps when installed on an M1 car. The heading creates no obligation of its own.
The rear lamp has position, stop and reversing functions, and each must meet geometric visibility angles once installed on an M1 car. Nothing may obstruct the light inside those angles.

requirements.text: No obstacle may lie inside the geometric visibility angles to the propagation of light from any part of the lamp's apparent surface observed from infinity. Obstacles already present at lamp type approval are not counted.
requirements.quote:
There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light
from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity.
requirements.reason: The rear position signalling function must be visible within the prescribed angles.

decisions.reason: This is a measurement rule for checking geometric visibility of the installed lamp. It applies to the rear lamp's visibility verification.

requirements.text: If visibility measurements are taken closer than infinity, shift the direction of observation parallel to achieve the same accuracy.
requirements.quote:
If measurements are taken closer to the lamp, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel to
achieve the same accuracy.
requirements.reason: The stop lamp function is subject to geometric visibility verification.

decisions.reason: Rear lamps are often partly covered by other vehicle parts once installed. If any part of the apparent surface is hidden, proof of photometric conformity of the visible part is required.

requirements.text: If any part of the lamp's apparent surface is hidden by other vehicle parts when installed, proof shall be furnished that the unhidden part still meets the photometric values prescribed for approval of the device.
requirements.quote:
proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the
photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
requirements.reason: The lamp is an exterior module installed on the vehicle, so partial obstruction by vehicle parts may occur.

results.reason: The rear lamp has LED modules on a PCB, so it is an ESA. Its stop lamp and rear position lamp are listed as immunity related functions in 2.12(c). Clause 6.8.1 therefore requires radiated immunity testing by a method chosen from Annex 9. The spec does not say whether the lamp has active control electronics, so this rests on the LED/PCB evidence.

Clause 6.8.2.1 sets the Table 2a severity over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band and the Table 2b minimum level over the whole band. The candidate keeps both conditions. It applies because the stop and rear position lamp functions are immunity related.

Clause 6.8.2.2 requires no degradation of immunity related functions during the Annex 9 tests. Stop lamp and rear position lamp operation are named in 2.12(c)(i), so the candidate matches the clause and the product.

Clause 6.9.1 requires ESA transient immunity testing per ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b and the ISO 16750-2 starting profile, using the Table 3a and 3b levels and status classes. The lamp has LED modules on a PCB and is powered from the vehicle supply. The candidate's "where applicable" wording keeps the starting profile limit. The spec does not show whether the lamp has active electronics, so this is slightly less certain.

Paragraph 3.2.5 applies only if an ESA is being type-approved under R10 and the Technical Service runs the test itself. The spec shows only LED modules on a PCB. It doesn't say the rear lamp is submitted for R10 ESA approval, or that it is an ESA subject to immunity or emission testing. The obligation is conditional and its applicability isn't established.

The marking requirement in 3.2.6 would apply to ESA samples submitted for R10 approval. The spec says nothing about an ESA approval route for this lamp. 'Exterior lighting & signalling module' alone doesn't show that R10 ESA approval applies, so applicability is unconfirmed.

Paragraph 3.2.7 is conditional ('where applicable') and concerns use restrictions for an ESA being approved under R10. The spec gives no use restrictions and no sign that ESA approval is sought. It is also unclear whether the lamp is an ESA at all, so applicability can't be decided.

results.reason: The rear lamp has position, stop and reversing functions, which are in R148 scope (paragraph 1). Paragraph 3.1.2.7(a) requires two complete samples unless otherwise specified. The candidate keeps the exception and the symmetrical left/right allowance.
Position, stop and reversing lamps are all listed in the R148 scope. Paragraph 3.2.1 requires a separate approval for each listed lamp, so the obligation applies to each function in the rear lamp.

The product is a combined or grouped unit of several lamps in one housing. Paragraph 3.2.2 allows approval only if each lamp meets R148 or another Regulation, and the candidate states this accurately. The retro-reflector falls under 'another Regulation'.

Paragraph 3.2.3 says approval is granted if the submitted lamp type meets R148. The interdependent-system same-applicant rule is worded conditionally ('if'), so the candidate keeps its limits. The spec does not say the lamps are interdependent, but the candidate does not assume they are.

R148 covers position, stop and reversing lamps, and the product has all three. Paragraph 3.3.2.1 requires the approval mark, which is a circle around "E" and the country's distinguishing number. The candidate keeps that wording.

Paragraph 3.3.2.2 requires the four to six-digit sequential number from the approval number, placed close to the approval mark. The product's R148 stop lamp function brings it into scope. The candidate keeps the source's conditions.

Paragraph 3.3.2.3 requires the symbols that identify the light-signalling lamps in paragraph 3.2.4. The product has rear position, stop and reversing functions, all within R148 scope. I did not read paragraph 3.2.4 itself, so the candidate's list of the product's three functions is an application of the clause and not a quote from it.

Paragraph 3.3.2.4 requires the Regulation number, then the letter 'R', then the two digits of the amendment series in force when the approval was issued. The product's R148 lamp functions bring it into scope. The candidate matches the clause.

R10 covers components and separate technical units (ESAs). Its definition of immunity-related functions names stop lamps and rear position lamps. The spec lists both functions plus LED modules on a PCB. Annex 9 2.1 requires ISO 11452-1 test conditions, and the candidate states this accurately. I did not check whether the manufacturer may choose a different test route.

The lamp is an ESA with immunity-related light functions. Annex 9 2.2 requires the ESA to be switched on and in normal operation, arranged as the Annex defines unless individual test methods dictate otherwise. The candidate keeps that exception.

Annex 9 2.4 is a general calibration-phase condition for any ESA under test. The lamp is such an ESA. The clause text matches the candidate. The product-specific reasoning (a supply or driver is needed) is an assumption, not a spec fact.

Annex 9 2.5 requires the test signal generating equipment and its layout to match the calibration phase. It applies to any ESA tested under Annex 9, including this lamp with LED electronics. The candidate's wording matches the clause.

Annex 9 3.1 sets the 20 to 6,000 MHz range and the AM, PM2 and PM3 modulations. The candidate reproduces these accurately. The 'if not otherwise agreed' condition is kept. It applies to an ESA with immunity-related lamp functions.

Annex 9 3.2 requires testing at ISO 11452-1 intervals over 20 to 6,000 MHz. It allows reduced spot frequencies if the manufacturer provides whole-band data from an ISO 17025 accredited laboratory recognised by the Type Approval Authority. The candidate preserves this condition. It applies to the lamp ESA.

Annex 9 3.3 requires that an ESA failing the tests be verified as failing under the relevant test conditions and not because of uncontrolled fields. It is a general Annex 9 requirement that applies to this lamp ESA. The candidate states it accurately.

results.reason: UN R10 covers ESAs, and clause 2.12(c) lists stop lamps and rear position lamps as immunity-related functions. Annex 9 4.2.2 requires ISO 11452-3 for TEM-cell testing, with the method chosen by the Technical Service. The candidate keeps the conditional "if TEM-cell is used" framing.

The lamp has rear position and stop functions, which clause 2.12(c) treats as immunity-related. Annex 9 4.3.2 gives the BCI options (ISO 11452-4 with substitution at 150 mm or closed loop at 900 mm, or in-vehicle ISO 11451-4 at 150 mm). The candidate reproduces these options and the conditional framing.

The lengths in the candidate match clause 4.3.2.1.2. However, the candidate asserts that the lamp has an LV harness only, and the spec says nothing about harnesses. The candidate also leaves out the closed-loop power-limitation straightness condition. The product facts needed to say which harness conditions apply are missing.

Clause 4.3.2.1.3 requires all harnesses to be placed on a low-permittivity material (εr≤1.4) at 50±5 mm above the ground plane. The candidate matches this and is conditional on BCI being used. The lamp is an electronic ESA with immunity-related functions.

Clause 4.3.2.1.5 requires the ESA case to be connected to the ground plane, directly or via a defined impedance, unless otherwise specified. The candidate keeps this wording and the BCI condition. The lamp is the ESA under test.
R148 scope covers position, stop and reversing lamps, and the product has all three. Paragraph 3.3.3.1 requires lamps to bear the approval marking, and the candidate states that.
The product's stop lamp, position lamp and reversing lamp fall within R148 scope. Paragraph 3.3.3.2 requires lamps to bear the applicant's trade name or mark, and the candidate states that.

The product is an R148 lamp with an outer lens and a housing. Paragraph 3.3.4.1 requires the approval marking to go on a part not designed to be separated from the light-emitting transparent part, and the candidate keeps that condition.

Paragraph 3.3.4.2 requires the approval marking to be visible when the lamp is fitted or when a movable part is opened. The candidate keeps the 'any prescribed' qualifier for LED substitute light source categories. The product is an M1 vehicle lamp in R148 scope.

Annex 7 3.3 allows an OATS complying with CISPR 16-1-4 as an alternative to an ALSE. The rear lamp's LED/PCB module is an electrical device intended to be part of a vehicle, so it fits the ESA definition in 2.8. The broadband exemption for ESAs without an oscillator above 9 kHz (6.10.1) covers only the narrowband requirements and Annexes 5 and 8. The spec does not describe the lamp's electronics, so some applicability doubt remains.

Annex 7 3.4 requires ambient noise to be at least 6 dB below the 6.5.2.1 limits, with the narrowband-transmission exception, and the candidate keeps both. The lamp's LED/PCB electronics make it a plausible ESA, though the spec gives no detail on them.
Annex 7 4.1 applies the limits across 30 to 1,000 MHz for ESA measurements in an ALSE or OATS. The wording matches, and the lamp is a plausible ESA.

Annex 7 4.2 allows quasi-peak or peak detectors and requires a 20 dB CISPR 12 correction when peak detectors are used, because the limits are quasi-peak limits. The candidate matches this and applies to the lamp as an ESA.

Annex 7 4.3 requires a spectrum analyser or scanning receiver using the Table 1 and 2 parameters. FFT-based instruments must meet CISPR 16-1-1, record continuously, and measure for at least 1 s per band. The candidate matches this.

Table 1 sets the spectrum analyser parameters for 30 to 1,000 MHz. Its note requires a video bandwidth of at least three times the RBW for peak measurements. The candidate keeps this condition, and the lamp is a plausible ESA.

Table 2 gives the scanning receiver parameters for 30 to 1,000 MHz: 120 kHz bandwidth, 60 kHz maximum step, and minimum dwell of 5 ms (peak) or 1 s (quasi-peak). The candidate matches these values. It omits the table's footnotes, but they do not change the core obligation.

Annex 7 4.4 tests the LV-harness-nearer-antenna configuration unless otherwise specified. It also requires testing at the CISPR 12 intervals, or the 14-band alternative with data from an accredited laboratory. The candidate preserves these conditions, and the lamp is a plausible ESA.
Annex 7 4.5 takes the maximum reading relative to the limit, across polarizations, in each of the 14 bands as the characteristic reading. The candidate matches this, and the lamp is a plausible ESA.

Annex 1 item 8 requires the number of the Technical Service's report in the communication. It applies because the product's lamp functions are within R148 scope.

Paragraph 3.1.1.3.1 is numbered as a sub-paragraph of 3.1.1.3, which covers retro-reflective marking plates. The text does not show whether it also covers retro-reflectors. The obligation is on the Type Approval Authority, not the product. It is unclear from the evidence that it applies to this retro-reflector.
Paragraph 3.2.1 requires a separate approval for each retro-reflective device listed in paragraph 1. Retro-reflectors are listed there, and the product contains one.
Paragraph 3.2.2 requires notice of approval, extension, refusal or withdrawal to be communicated on a form conforming to the Annex 1 model. This applies to an approved retro-reflector type.
Paragraph 3.2.3 requires the approval number assigned to each approved type to be marked on the device following paragraph 3.3. This applies to the retro-reflector.

The R150 scope covers class IA and IB retro-reflectors, and the product has a retro-reflector. Paragraph 3.2.5 requires the class symbol to be referenced in Annex 1. The candidate states this in general terms, and the symbols themselves are in Table 1.

Table 1 gives IB for a motor-vehicle retro-reflector combined with signal lamps that are not watertight, IA if independent, and a minimum 'a' of 5 mm. The product's retro-reflector is combined with signal lamps in one housing. The candidate keeps the 'not watertight' condition. The spec does not say whether the lamp is watertight, but it lists a seal/gasket, so that point is uncertain.
Paragraph 3.2.6 says the change index for each device follows the series of amendments, and the values are in Table 2. The product has a retro-reflector, which is a device covered by that table.

Table 2 gives change index 0 for the 00 series and 1 for the 01 series for the combined motor-vehicle retro-reflector. The candidate drops the 'not watertight' qualifier, and the spec does not say whether the lamp is watertight. The product is a combined retro-reflector, so the match is acceptable with lower confidence.
Paragraph 3.3.1.1 requires every device of an approved type to have enough space for the Unique Identifier or approval marking and the other markings. The product's retro-reflector is such a device.
Paragraph 3.3.1.2 requires all markings to be clearly legible and indelible. It applies to the retro-reflector device.
Paragraph 3.3.1.3 sets the approval marking size 'a' from Table 1, which gives 5 mm for classes IA and IB. The candidate states this correctly for the product's retro-reflector.
Paragraph 3.3.2.1 requires the approval mark, a circle around the letter E followed by the distinguishing number of the approving country. It applies to the retro-reflector.
Paragraph 3.3.2.2 requires the four to six-digit sequential number of the approval number to be placed close to the approval mark. It applies to the retro-reflector.
Clause 4.1.4 applies to the outer surface of retro-reflective devices. The product has an integrated retro-reflector, and the candidate restates the clause without changing its meaning.
Clause 4.1.5 bars access to the inner surface of retro-reflectors in normal use. The product has a retro-reflector, and the wording matches the clause.

Clause 4.1.6.1 only covers retro-reflectors that combine an optical unit and a filter. The candidate keeps that condition, but the spec does not say whether this retro-reflector has a filter. It lists only a molded PMMA prism retro-reflector and a separate red outer lens.

Clause 4.1.6.2 bans colouring retro-reflecting optical units and filters with paint or varnish. This is an unconditional prohibition and applies to the product's retro-reflector. The spec does not say how the retro-reflector is coloured, but that does not change the requirement.

Clause 4.2.1.2 sets the night-time colour test with Illuminant A and the R48 limits. Clause 4.2.1.1 limits it to white, red or amber devices, and the candidate leaves that out. A rear retro-reflector on an M1 is normally red, so the omission is likely harmless. The spec does not state the retro-reflector's colour, which lowers confidence.

The product has a retro-reflector in a multi-function rear lamp housing. UN R150 Annex 5 item 9 asks for a concise description with these entries: in isolation or part of an assembly, colour, integral installation in a lamp, geometric conditions (if any), and the ≤750 mm mounting height. The candidate keeps these entries. It drops the "if any" qualifier on geometric conditions, which is a small omission.

Annex 5 item 10 of the R150 communication requires the position of the approval mark or UI. The product's retro-reflector falls within R150's scope as a retro-reflector device. The spec does not say whether it is approved separately, which lowers confidence slightly.

The product has a PMMA prism retro-reflector built into the rear lamp. That falls within UN R150's scope of retro-reflectors, and I did not check R150's rules for retro-reflectors combined with lamps. The cited clause (Annex 5 / Part 1 / 1.1 in the source labelling) requires a check for mirror effect by slightly turning the device when RI is measured at β1 = β2 = 0°. If there is a mirror effect, the reading is taken at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°. The candidate states this condition and fallback accurately. The only caveat is that the clause is a test-procedure step, not a design requirement.

The product has a rear retro-reflector. R150 5.1.1 sets the shape, photometric/colour and physical/mechanical requirements for Class IA/IB retro-reflectors, and the candidate keeps the "depending on materials and construction" condition. The spec does not state the class, but a rear retro-reflector on an M1 car would normally be IA or IB.

5.1.2 requires the applicant to submit ten samples, tested in the order given in 5.1.7. The product's retro-reflector would be approved under R150, so this applies. The class assumption is the same as for 5.1.1.

5.1.3.1 sets the test sequence: heat resistance, then colorimetric and RI examination at least one hour later, then the group tests. The candidate summarises this faithfully. It leaves out the step where the min/max samples are fully tested, which does not change the obligation.
5.1.3.2.1 requires each group to have a colour meeting 5.1.5 after the tests. The candidate matches this, and the product has a retro-reflector.
5.1.3.2.2 requires an RI meeting 5.1.4, verified at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0°, or in all Annex 4 Part 1 positions 1.1 and 1.2 if necessary. The candidate keeps this condition.
5.1.4.1 requires the applicant to specify one or more axes of reference, or a range, corresponding to β1 = β2 = 0°. The product's retro-reflector is subject to approval, so this applies.
5.1.4.2 is conditional: photometric measurements are repeated for each axis, or for the extreme axes of a range, when more than one axis or a range is specified. The candidate keeps that condition.
