results.reason: Annex 8, paragraph 2.1.2 of UN R148 says an LED-only lamp function is deemed to meet the intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured under paragraph 1.2 comply. The candidate keeps that condition. The product's position, stop and reversing functions fall within R148's scope. The spec lists the light source as "LED modules on PCB" and names no other light-generating technology. It does not say per function that LED is the only technology, so "LED only" is a reasonable but not explicit reading. I did not read paragraph 1.2 itself.

The product has a retro-reflector, which is in R150 scope. Clause 1.1 sets the mechanical and geometric conformity criterion: differences must not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations. The reference to the approved type is a mild paraphrase.

Clause 1.2 sets the photometric conformity criterion for mass-produced retro-reflective devices: no measured value may deviate unfavourably by more than 20% from the prescribed minimum. This applies to the lamp's retro-reflector.
Clause 1.3 states that the chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with. This applies to the retro-reflector.

The clause requires the approval mark holder to carry out at least the specified tests at appropriate intervals, in accordance with the Regulation. It also requires further sampling and corrective steps if non-conformity is found. The candidate preserves this.
Clause 2.1 says conformity tests cover photometric and colorimetric characteristics and resistance to penetration of water. This applies to the retro-reflector type.
Clause 2.2.1 says tests shall generally follow the methods in the Regulation. The candidate keeps the word "generally".
Clause 2.2.2 allows equivalent methods only with the Type Approval Authority's consent. It makes the manufacturer responsible for proving equivalence. The candidate matches this.
Clause 2.2.3 requires regular calibration of test apparatus and its correlation with the Type Approval Authority's measurements. The candidate matches this.
Clause 2.2.4 says the reference methods are always those of the Regulation, particularly for administrative verification and sampling. The candidate matches this.
Clause 2.3 requires random sampling from a uniform batch of the same type, defined by the manufacturer's production methods. The candidate matches this and applies to the retro-reflector.

Annex 5 Part 3 paragraph 1.1 sits under the heading "Shape and dimensions of retro-reflective devices of Class IA or IB". It says the illuminating surfaces must not be easily confused with the triangular shape from 10 m. The triangular shape is the one prescribed for Class IIIA/IIIB in paragraph 2.1, which the candidate cites correctly. The spec says the rear lamp is an M1 car lamp with an integrated retro-reflector, which would be a Class IA/IB device. The spec does not state the class, so that part is inferred. The candidate also leaves out the Class IA/IB scope, but the obligation itself matches the clause.

R150 covers Class IA/IB retro-reflectors. The product has a moulded PMMA prism retro-reflector, so the Annex 6 Part 1 heat procedure (48 h dry at 65±2 °C, then 1 h cooling at 23±2 °C) applies. The spec does not state the reflector class, but a rear non-triangular retro-reflector on an M1 vehicle would be IA or IB.

The clause requires no visible cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device, especially its optical component, after the heat test. This applies to the product's retro-reflector and the wording matches the clause.

The clause covers retro-reflective devices whether or not they are part of a lamp, so the reflector integrated in the rear lamp is in scope. The candidate preserves the 50±5 °C immersion for 10 min, the 20 mm depth, the 180° repeat and the immediate 25±5 °C immersion.

The clause requires that no water reaches the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit, and that visible water means failure. This applies to the product's retro-reflector, and the candidate wording matches the clause.

Clause 5.1.4.3 sets the photometric measurement area for Class IA/IB retro-reflectors: a 200 mm circle, limited to 100 cm², with the manufacturer specifying the perimeter. The product has a retro-reflector, and Class IA/IB is the likely class for an M1 rear retro-reflector. The spec does not state the class.

Clause 5.1.4.4.1 requires red Class IA/IB retro-reflectors to meet the Table 3 RI minimums when measured per Annex 4 Part 1 para 3. The spec does not state the retro-reflector's colour or class. A rear retro-reflector is red under R48, so the match is plausible.

The Table 3 red IA/IB values are correct: 300/200/100 mcd/lx at 20' and 5/2.8/2.5 mcd/lx at 1°30'. The last sentence about the solid angle copies a source note whose 'last two columns' are blank ('--') for IA/IB. That note really applies to Class IV, so the candidate overreaches on that point. The core minimum-RI obligation is supported.
Clause 5.1.5.1 requires the night-time colour test of the retro-reflector to follow the para 4.2.1 method. The product has a retro-reflector.

Clause 5.1.5.2 requires the reflected light's trichromatic coordinates to be within the UN R48 night-time colour limits. Specifying red for a rear retro-reflector is a reasonable application, though the spec does not state the colour.

The Table 4 first row (5.1.7) requires a general specifications visual inspection on all samples, a–j. This applies to type approval of Class IA/IB retro-reflectors. The product's retro-reflector class is not stated, but IA/IB is plausible for M1.

The Table 4 sequence in the clause matches the candidate: shapes and dimensions, heat, colorimetry, photometry, water, fuels, oils, corrosion, rear face, stability in time, and weathering, with intermediate colorimetry and photometry checks. It applies to Class IA/IB samples. The product's retro-reflector class is not stated.

The product has a retro-reflector, and UN R150 covers retro-reflectors. Clause 3.6 sets the photometric measuring distance: it must respect the δ, γ and η angle limits and be at least 10 m. The candidate states this accurately. The spec does not give the retro-reflector class, but the clause is a test-method rule that applies to retro-reflectors in general.

Clause 3.7 requires sufficiently uniform illuminance over the useful area of the retro-reflective device. It is checked with a measuring element of at most one-tenth of the examined area, and max/min must be ≤ 1.05. The candidate preserves this, and the product's retro-reflector is within R150 scope.

Clause 3.8.1 requires the photometer head to be corrected to the CIE photopic spectral luminous efficiency. This is a test-equipment condition for photometry of the retro-reflector, and the candidate matches the clause.

Clause 3.8.2 requires no perceptible change in local sensitivity within the aperture, and otherwise requires suitable provisions such as a diffusing window. The candidate preserves this condition and example. It applies to the retro-reflector's photometric testing.

Clause 4.1.1 requires the photometer head's field of view and the spread of light from the sample and the source to be restricted as much as possible. The candidate omits the matt-black background and sample-holder recommendation, but it does not contradict the clause. It applies to retro-reflector measurement.
Clause 4.1.2 requires floor and wall reflections to be screened from both the sample and the photometer head by baffles. The candidate matches this. It applies to retro-reflector measurement.

Clause 4.1.3 allows for residual stray light by measuring it with the sample covered. The cover can be an opaque matt black surface, zigzag folded black paper of the same size and shape, or a suitably oriented specular black surface with a light trap. The value is then subtracted from the retro-reflector measurement. The candidate preserves this.

The rear lamp has a retro-reflector, and R150 covers retro-reflectors (Classes IA/IB for M1 rear). Annex 5 Part 1 §1.2 applies to devices not marked "TOP". The candidate keeps that condition and the ±5° allowance if the value is not reached. It drops the 20' divergence and β details, which is a minor omission.

§1.3 applies to retro-reflective devices marked "TOP". The candidate keeps that condition, and the spec doesn't say whether the retro-reflector is marked. The procedure and the rule that RI must not fall below the prescribed value are faithfully stated.
§1.4 is a general RI measurement rule for retro-reflective devices. The candidate keeps its condition: RI at β=0° and ε=0° exceeds the specified value by 50% or more.
§3.1 requires the CIE-angular system (Figure A4-I) for specifying and measuring retro-reflective devices. This applies to the product's retro-reflector.
§3.3 requires illumination with CIE Standard Illuminant A and measurement as in Part 1 of Annex 4 when testing retro-reflection. This applies to the retro-reflector.
§3.4 sets the measuring geometry limits δ≤10', γ≤10' and η≤80'. The candidate states them correctly, and they apply to photometry of the retro-reflector.
§3.5 says stray reflections should be avoided by appropriate masking during photometric measurements. The candidate states this as a measurement practice for the retro-reflector, which is acceptable.
R150 covers retro-reflectors, and the product has an integrated retro-reflector. Annex 5 para 2.4 requires photometric and chromaticity measurement of the sampled device.

Annex 5 para 2.5 makes the manufacturer responsible for the statistical study and for acceptability criteria agreed with the approval authority. The candidate omits the 95% confidence detail but does not contradict it.
Para 1.2.1 sets the 20% unfavourable-deviation limit from the prescribed minimum values for conformity of retro-reflective devices. This applies to the product's retro-reflector.
Para 1.3 states that the chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with. It applies to the retro-reflector.

Paras 2 and 2.2 cover the first sampling of four devices (samples A and B). If any specimen deviates by more than 20%, the manufacturer must align production and a repeated sampling follows within two months.
Para 3.1 states that conformity is not contested if no specimen of samples C and D deviates by more than 20%.
Para 3.2 is the stem for the contested-conformity criteria, which are listed in 3.2.1 and 3.2.2. The candidate summarises them acceptably, though 3.2 itself gives only the lead-in.
Para 3.2.1 covers one C or D specimen above 20% with none above 30%. It requires realignment and a second repeated sampling within two months.
Para 3.2.2 states that approval is withdrawn if one specimen of C and D deviates by more than 30%.
Para 4.1 states that conformity is not contested if no specimen of samples E and F deviates by more than 20%.
Para 4.2 states that approval is withdrawn if at least one specimen of samples E or F deviates by more than 20%.

Para 6.1 requires one retro-reflector of sample A to pass the Annex 6 Part 2 para 1 water-penetration test. If it fails, both devices of sample B must be tested and both must pass. The advance warning triangle variant does not apply to this product.

The product has a retro-reflector inside a combined rear lamp housing. UN R150 covers retro-reflectors. Annex 6 Part 4 point 2 says that when the device is combined with a light, the lamp is the sample put through the saline mist test. Point 4.1 then requires that, immediately after the test, the sample shows no excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device. The candidate keeps this condition and adds nothing from other clauses. The spec does not state the retro-reflector's R150 class, so some uncertainty remains.

The clause applies to retro-reflectors, and the rear lamp has one. But the clause sits under paragraph 1.3, which says the RI measurement applies only if visual inspection does not reveal water, or in case of doubt. The candidate drops that condition and says to measure RI after the water-penetration test, with no condition attached. That is broader than the source. Under 1.2, visible water means the device fails, and no RI measurement is then called for.

R23 applies to reversing lamps for M and N vehicles, and the product is an M1 rear lamp with a reversing lamp. Clause 2.1 says the applicant must be the trade-name or mark holder or their accredited representative. The candidate leaves out the optional installation-inclination provision, but that omission doesn't contradict the clause.

Clause 2.2.1 requires drawings in triplicate that identify the lamp type. They must show the mounting position, the axis of reference, the centre of reference, and the approval-mark position. The product has a reversing lamp, so this applies. The manoeuvring-lamp additions don't apply to a reversing lamp, and the candidate leaves them out correctly.

Clause 2.2.2 requires a brief technical description. It must give the filament lamp category, the LED light source category, or the light source module identification code, except for lamps with non-replaceable light sources. The product uses LED modules. The spec doesn't say whether they are replaceable, and the candidate keeps the exception.

Clause 2.2.3 requires two samples. If the devices are symmetrical but not identical, the two samples may be identical and made for one side only. The candidate's wording matches this and applies to the reversing lamp. It describes the symmetrical case a little loosely, but the meaning is the same.

Annex 7 Part 2 point 1.1 applies to moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA. It requires the outer and illuminating surface to be wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil. After about 5 minutes the surface is cleaned, then RI is measured per 5.1.3.2.2. The product has a moulded PMMA prism retro-reflector, so the procedure fits. The spec doesn't state the reflector class, but any rear retro-reflector would fall within the listed classes. The candidate leaves out "lightly", which is a minor omission.

The product includes a reversing lamp, which UN R23 6.1 covers. Clause 6.1.1 requires intensity within the minima and maxima, measured relative to the axis of reference. The candidate keeps that meaning.
The product has a reversing lamp. Clause 6.1.2 sets a minimum of 80 cd along the axis of reference, and the candidate matches it.
The product has a reversing lamp. The candidate states the maxima from 6.1.3 correctly: 300 cd in or above the horizontal plane, 600 cd between h-h and 5° D, and 8,000 cd below 5° D.

The product has a reversing lamp, so the annex 3 minima apply under 6.1.4. The candidate keeps the exception: verification only up to 30° inwards at 25 cd or more is allowed only for lamps installed exclusively in a pair. It also keeps the requirement to declare this in the application and the communication form. The spec does not say whether the lamp is paired, but the candidate states this as a condition, so it is not an invented fact.

The product is a multi-function rear lamp in one housing that includes a reversing lamp, which R23 covers. Paragraph 4.5 requires each lamp in a grouped or combined assembly to satisfy R23 or another Regulation. The candidate keeps that obligation and its exclusion rule.

Paragraph 4.5.1 permits a single approval mark on combined lamps that comply with several Regulations. The candidate keeps it permissive ("may") and keeps the visibility and non-removability conditions. The product is a combined assembly.
Paragraph 4.5.1.1 requires the single approval mark to be visible after installation. This applies to the combined rear lamp if it uses a single mark, and the candidate states it that way.
Paragraph 4.5.1.2 says no light-transmitting part of the combined lamps can be removed without also removing the mark. The outer lens is a light-transmitting part of the product, so this fits.

Paragraph 4.5.2 requires an identification symbol for each lamp under each approving Regulation, with the series of amendments. The product combines a reversing lamp with other lamps. The candidate leaves out the placement options in 4.5.2.1 and 4.5.2.2, but this does not contradict the clause.

The product includes a reversing lamp, which falls under R23. Paragraph 10.1 lets the approval be withdrawn if the requirements are not met or if lamps bearing the mark do not conform to the approved type. The candidate's "carry the approval marks" wording is a slight stretch, but the clause refers to the marking requirements in paragraphs 4.3.1 and 4.3.2 and to lamps bearing the mark.

Paragraph 11 requires an approval holder who completely ceases to manufacture an approved type of reversing lamp to inform the approving authority. The product has a reversing lamp function, so the obligation applies conditionally to its approval holder. The candidate keeps the "completely ceases" condition. The spec does not say who holds the approval, so applicability rests on that assumption.

R23 applies to the reversing lamp in this M1 rear lamp. Paragraph 3.1 requires lamps submitted for approval to bear the applicant's trade name or mark, clearly legible and indelible. The candidate keeps that wording.

Paragraph 3.4 requires adequate space for the approval mark and the 4.3 additional symbols. It also requires that space to be shown in the 2.2.1 drawing. The candidate keeps both points, and the reversing lamp is in scope.

Paragraph 4.1 says approval shall be granted if the two samples meet the requirements. That is a sufficient condition and a duty on the approving authority. The candidate rewrites it as 'granted only if', a necessary condition the clause does not state. It also presents this as a product obligation.

Paragraph 4.3 and 4.3.1 require every approved reversing lamp to bear, in the reserved space, an international approval mark. The mark is a circle with E and the country number, plus an approval number. This comes in addition to the marks in 3.1–3.3 or 3.5. The product includes a reversing lamp.

Paragraph 4.3.2 requires the additional symbol of letters A and R, arranged as shown in Annex 2. It applies to approved reversing lamps, and the product has one. The ML symbol for manoeuvring lamps does not apply here.

The product combines position, stop and reversing lamps in one housing. Clause 4.5.2.1 gives marking on the light-emitting surface as one of two options. The other option is a group mark under 4.5.2.2, which the candidate also states.
Clause 4.5.2.2 requires a group mark that lets each grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp be clearly identified. This fits the combined housing.

Clause 4.5.3 sets a minimum size for the components of a single approval mark on combined lamps. It applies only if the product carries a single approval mark, which the spec doesn't state, but the candidate's wording keeps that condition.

Clause 4.5.4 requires an approval number for each approved type and bars the same Contracting Party from reusing it for another type of grouped or combined lamps. The product is a combined lamp that includes a reversing lamp, so this applies.
Clause 4.6 requires the mark and symbol to be indelible and clearly legible when the reversing lamp is mounted on the vehicle. The product includes a reversing lamp.

Clause 5 applies the R48/R86 general and individual specifications, and their annexes, to each lamp and vehicle category where verification at type approval is feasible. The product is an M1 lamp with a reversing function, and the candidate keeps the feasibility condition.
Clause 5.1 requires each sample to conform to the specifications that follow. It is a general requirement that applies to the reversing lamp type.
Clause 5.2 requires reversing lamps to keep working satisfactorily and keep their prescribed characteristics in normal use despite vibration. The product has a reversing lamp.

The product includes a reversing lamp, and R23 Annex 1 item 9 sets out the concise description in the approval communication for a reversing lamp. That description covers the number, category and kind of light source, voltage and wattage, control gear, light source module and installation conditions. The candidate keeps these items. The spec shows LED modules, so the light source entry applies. The manoeuvring-lamp items are not mentioned, which is acceptable because they do not apply to this product.

Annex 1 item 10 of the R23 communication requires the position of the approval mark. The product contains a reversing lamp, so its R23 approval communication would carry this item. The candidate matches the clause wording.

Annex 1 item 11 of the R23 communication has a comment for reversing lamps: whether the device is installed only as part of a pair, yes or no. The product has a reversing lamp, so the comment applies. The candidate states it as a yes/no entry, which matches the clause. The spec does not say whether the lamp is installed in pairs, but the candidate only requires the statement.

Para 6.1.5 (R23 reversing lamp intensity) caps maximum intensities with all sources lit in a single lamp that has more than one light source. The candidate keeps that condition. The product has a reversing lamp and LED modules (plural), so the conditional obligation plausibly applies. The spec does not state the number of sources in the reversing function.

Para 6.1.6.2 requires either the Annex 3 minimum intensity or a failure tell-tale at 50% or more of the minimum on the axis of reference, with a communication-form note. The candidate preserves both options and the condition of more than one light source. The reversing lamp uses LED modules, so the conditional obligation plausibly applies. The number of sources is not confirmed in the spec.

Para 7.1 states that all photometric and colorimetric measurements are made under the conditions that follow in 7.1.1 to 7.1.4. R23 covers reversing lamps, and the product includes one. The candidate's reference to 7.1.1 to 7.1.4 matches the sub-paragraphs. Which sub-paragraph applies depends on the light source and control gear type.

The product has a reversing lamp, which is in R23 scope, and LED modules on a PCB. The clause only requires control gear where it is needed to supply the light source. The spec does not mention control gear, so this is a moderate-confidence match.
The reversing lamp is in R23 scope, and the clause requires the applied voltage to be stated in the Annex 1 communication form.
The LED light source is not a filament lamp, so the clause applies. The wording keeps the 1 minute and 10 minute checks, the HV ratio method and the 3% in 15 minutes stability definition.
The clause requires the apparent surface limits of a light-signalling device to be determined along the reference axis. The reversing lamp is covered by R23.

The reversing lamp must emit white light inside the Annex 3 grid, with no sharp colour variation outside it. The non-replaceable light source verification condition is kept. The LED modules are non-replaceable only if the BOM confirms it, but the candidate states this conditionally.
Conformity of production applies to series-produced lamps approved under R23. The candidate matches the clause's reference to Appendix 2 of the Agreement.
Lamps must be manufactured to conform to the approved type, with compliance to paragraphs 6 and 8 verified. This applies to the approved reversing lamp.
Clause 9.1.1 requires compliance with the Annex 4 minimum conformity of production control requirements, and the candidate states this.
Clause 9.1.2 requires compliance with the Annex 5 minimum sampling requirements, and the candidate states this.

The clause lets the approval authority verify conformity control methods at any time, with a normal frequency of once every two years. Restating this as production facilities having to allow verification is a reasonable reading.

The spec describes a single housing combining a rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp. Figure 2 and its note give simplified marking models B, C and D for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, including the reversing lamp (AR) approved under R23. The wording keeps the "possible" (optional) character of the models. The clause is an example, so the match is only moderately strong.
Annex 3 1.1 requires stray reflections to be avoided by appropriate masking during photometric measurements. This applies to testing the product's reversing lamp function.

Annex 3 1.2 sets the conditions for measurements when results are challenged: inverse-square distance, a receiver angle of 10' to 1°, and a 1/4° tolerance on direction. The candidate keeps the condition "if results are challenged". It applies to the reversing lamp.

results.reason: The product has a reversing lamp, which R23 covers. Annex 4 §2 requires the approval mark holder to run minimum tests and to take further samples and act on non-conformity. The candidate keeps those conditions.
R23 Annex 4 §2.1 limits conformity tests to photometric and colorimetric characteristics, and the reversing lamp is in scope. The candidate matches that.
Annex 4 §2.2.1 says tests are generally carried out by the methods in the Regulation. The candidate matches and the reversing lamp is in scope.
Annex 4 §2.2.2 allows equivalent methods only with the competent authority's consent, and the manufacturer must prove equivalence. The candidate keeps both conditions.
Annex 4 §2.2.3 requires regular calibration of test apparatus and its correlation with the competent authority's measurements. The candidate matches.
Annex 4 §2.2.4 says the Regulation's methods are the reference methods, particularly for administrative verification and sampling. The candidate matches.

Annex 4 §2.3 requires random sampling from a uniform batch and defines the batch as lamps of the same type. The candidate omits the optional grouping of factory records, which does not change the obligation.
Annex 4 §2.4 requires photometric measurement of the sampled lamp at the Annex 3 minimum-value points and for the chromaticity coordinates. The candidate matches and the reversing lamp is in scope.

Annex 4 §2.5 makes the manufacturer responsible for a statistical study and for acceptability criteria agreed with the authority. The criteria must give 95% confidence of at least 0.95 probability of passing an Annex 5 first-sampling spot check. The candidate preserves this.

UN R26 applies to external projections of M1 vehicles, and the spec says the product is an exterior rear lamp on an M1 car. Paragraph 5.2 states the obligation as proposed. The 5.1 exclusions (above 2 m, below the floor line, or out of reach of a 100 mm sphere) depend on mounting position, which the spec doesn't give. They don't clearly remove the lamp from scope.

Paragraph 5.3 bans outward-directed parts likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists. This applies to the external surface of an M1 vehicle, which includes the exterior rear lamp. The wording matches the clause. The 5.1 location exclusions are not confirmed either way.

Paragraph 5.4 sets a minimum 2.5 mm radius of curvature for protruding parts. Parts protruding less than 5 mm are exempt, but their outward-facing angles must be blunted unless they protrude less than 1.5 mm. The candidate keeps these limits. The separate soft-material exception in 5.5 (60 Shore A or less) is not part of 5.4. The lamp is external equipment on an M1 vehicle, so the clause applies.
The product has a reversing lamp, so R23 applies. Annex 5 para 3.1 gives the 20 per cent limit for samples C and D and the 0 per cent closure rule for sample C. The candidate keeps both.
R23 applies to the reversing lamp. Para 3.2 is a lead-in saying conformity is contested if the deviations in its sub-paragraphs occur, and the candidate says the same.
The candidate matches para 3.2.1: one specimen above 20 per cent but none above 30 per cent, then alignment, a second sampling within two months, and samples C and D retained until the process ends.
The candidate matches para 3.2.2: a deviation above 30 per cent means approval is withdrawn and paragraph 5 applies. R23 applies to the reversing lamp.
The candidate matches para 4: four lamps are selected at random from stock made after alignment, and the two pairs are marked E and F.
The candidate matches para 4.1: the 20 per cent limit for samples E and F, and the 0 per cent closure rule for sample E.
The candidate matches para 4.2: a deviation above 20 per cent in any specimen of E or F contests conformity, approval is withdrawn, and paragraph 5 applies.
The candidate matches para 5: approval is withdrawn under paragraph 10 of the Regulation. R23 approval applies to the reversing lamp.

The product has a reversing lamp, which R23 covers. Annex 3 para 2.2 sets the 50% check for substantial local intensity variations between prescribed measurement directions. The candidate keeps the condition and the limit.

The clause applies only to lamps equipped with several light sources. The spec says "LED modules on PCB" for the whole lamp. It does not say the reversing lamp has several light sources. The clause text is also only a heading ending in a colon, with the sub-paragraphs given separately.

The clause applies to multi-source lamps with non-replaceable light sources. The spec does not say whether the LED modules are replaceable. It also does not say the reversing lamp has several sources. Both facts are inferred, not stated.

Annex 4 para 1.1 is the conformity-of-production criterion for mechanical and geometric conformity of reversing lamps. The candidate reproduces it accurately. The spec does not state series production, but the product is a production lamp.

Annex 4 paras 1.2 and 1.2.1 set the 20% unfavourable-deviation criterion for photometric conformity of mass-produced lamps tested at random under para 7. This applies to the reversing lamp, and the candidate preserves the condition.

Annex 4 para 1.3 requires the chromaticity coordinates to be met when tested under para 7. This applies to the reversing lamp. The spec's evidence cites the red outer lens, which relates to the other functions, but the obligation itself fits the reversing lamp.
The product has a reversing lamp, which is within R23. Annex 5 1.1 says mechanical and geometric conformity holds if differences stay within inevitable manufacturing deviations.

The clause covers photometric conformity of mass-produced lamps, tested per paragraph 7 against paragraph 6, using a lamp chosen at random. The clause text is truncated and continues in 1.2.1 and following lines, but the candidate does not contradict it.
The clause requires the paragraph 1.2.1 requirements of Annex 4 to be met, as the candidate states. It applies to the reversing lamp. I did not read Annex 4 1.2.1 itself.
The clause states that lamps with apparent defects are disregarded in this conformity check. It applies to reversing lamp sampling.
The clause requires chromaticity coordinates to comply when tested under paragraph 7. The reversing lamp is covered.
The clause describes the first sampling of four random lamps, marked as samples A and B of two each. It applies to R23 lamps in production.

The clause says conformity is not contested if no specimen of A and B deviates by more than 20 per cent. It also says measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample A deviate by no more than 0 per cent. The candidate keeps both points.

The clause says conformity is contested if at least one specimen deviates by more than 20 per cent. The manufacturer must then align production, and repeated sampling follows within two months of notification. Samples A and B are kept until the process ends, and the candidate omits only that the Technical Service keeps them.
The clause provides for four lamps selected at random from stock made after alignment, marked as samples C and D of two each. It applies to reversing lamp production.

UN R26 applies to external projections of M1 vehicles, and the spec says the product is an M1 rear lamp. R26 para 2.3 includes lighting and light-signalling devices in the "external surface". Para 2.8 defines the dimension of a projection by the Annex 3 para 2 method. Annex 3 para 2.2 sets the 100 mm sphere method for components on a non-convex surface whose projection can't be measured simply. The candidate keeps that condition. R48 applies to M-category vehicles, and the rear position lamp has a width position. Paragraph 5.8.3 gives the method for finding that position: outer edge for overall width, inner edges for distance between lamps. It also allows skipping exact edge determination where compliance is clear. The candidate keeps all of this. It is a measurement rule, so the match is only moderately strong.

Paragraph 5.9 applies to any lamp while it is switched ON. The product's position, stop and reversing lamps are such lamps. The candidate keeps the condition 'in the absence of specific instructions'.

Paragraph 5.9.2 permits photometric variation due to ambient light, other lamps switching, or use for another function. Any variation must still meet the lamp's technical provisions. The product combines several functions in one module, so the clause is relevant. The candidate keeps the proviso.

Paragraph 5.10.1 says red light from a rear-fitted lamp must not be visible from the front. The product is a rear lamp with a red-tinted lens on an M1 vehicle, so it applies. The candidate states the obligation accurately.

Paragraph 5.14.1 prohibits concealing lamps. Only main-beam, dipped-beam and front fog lamps are excepted. The rear position, stop and reversing lamps are not excepted, so they must not be concealable. R48 covers M1 vehicles, and the candidate keeps the exception.

The paragraph 5.15 colour table gives rear position lamp red, stop lamp red, reversing lamp white, and rear retro-reflector red (triangular and non-triangular). The product has all four of these functions, and the candidate states the colours correctly.

Paragraph 5.16.1 requires the number of lamps on the vehicle to equal the number in the individual specifications. This is a vehicle-level installation rule. It applies to the position, stop and reversing functions this module provides. The product spec gives no lamp counts, so the candidate only restates the clause and sets no specific number.

R48 applies to M/N vehicles, and the product is an M1 rear lamp with red rear position and stop lamps. Clause 5.10.4.1 prohibits direct visibility of a red lamp's apparent surface from the front within Zone 1 at 25 m. The candidate keeps the red rearmost side-marker exception.

Clause 5.10.4.3 is the 0.25 cd per lamp deemed-compliance rule for red light to the front, and it covers the red stop and position lamps. The candidate drops the white-to-rear part for the reversing lamp. That follows from the reversing-lamp exception in 5.10.4.2, which the context shows.

Clause 5.11 requires the rear position lamps to switch ON and OFF only simultaneously with the front position lamps, end-outline and side-marker lamps (if they exist) and the rear registration plate lamp. The product has a rear position lamp. The exceptions in 5.11.1 are a separate sub-clause and are not stated in the candidate, so I rate this with slightly lower confidence.

Paragraph 5.27 applies to M and N vehicles and covers devices 2.5.4 (stop lamp) and 2.5.7 (rear position lamp). The M1 rear lamp has both functions. The candidate keeps the constant-voltage condition and the applicant's demonstration to the Technical Service.

Paragraph 5.27.2 is the correct source for the voltage limit. However, 5.27.3 disapplies 5.27.1 and 5.27.2 for devices with electronic light source control gear, a variable intensity control, or only UN R128-approved light sources. The candidate text omits this exception. The spec says only 'LED modules on PCB' and does not say whether the lamp has control gear or R128-approved sources, so applicability cannot be confirmed.

Paragraph 5.27.4 requires a report on the compliance methods and results to be attached to the approval documentation. This follows from the 5.27 demonstration that applies to the product's stop and rear position lamp functions. The candidate's wording matches the source.

R48 applies to M and N vehicles, and the product is an M1 rear lamp with a reversing function. Clause 6.4.6.1, under Orientation, says the reversing lamp is oriented rearwards. The candidate keeps that meaning.

Clause 6.4.7.1 sets the electrical connection rule for the reversing lamp. The lamp switches ON only if reverse gear is engaged and the propulsion control position allows propulsion operation. It must not switch ON or stay ON if either condition fails. The candidate restates this accurately, and the product has a reversing lamp.

Clause 6.4.8 makes a reversing lamp tell-tale optional. It makes a failure tell-tale mandatory only if the component regulation requires one. The candidate keeps that condition, and the product has a reversing lamp.
Paragraph 5.28.1 applies to lamps installed on M and N vehicles, and this is an M1 rear lamp. The candidate keeps the exception for obstacles that already existed at lamp type approval.

Paragraph 5.28.2 is a conditional measurement rule for verifying geometric visibility of installed lamps. The stop lamp is one of those lamps. The candidate keeps the condition (measurement closer than infinity) and the parallel-shift requirement.

Paragraph 5.28.3 applies to any installed lamp. It is conditional on part of the apparent surface being hidden by other vehicle parts, and the candidate keeps that condition and the proof requirement. The product evidence cited (reversing function) is weak, but the clause applies to the lamp as a whole.

The product uses LED modules, and paragraph 5.29 allows an LED module to be non-replaceable if the communication sheet of the component type approval says so. The candidate's wording ('only if') is a slightly stronger reading but keeps the condition. The spec does not say whether the modules are replaceable.

Paragraph 5.30 requires installed lamps (devices) to be type approved under the device Regulations listed in paragraph 6, where applicable. The product combines rear position, stop and reversing lamps and a retro-reflector, and the candidate keeps the 'where applicable' qualifier. I did not read paragraph 6 to confirm which device Regulations cover each of these devices.
Paragraph 5.3 applies to all light-signalling devices on M and N vehicles. The rear lamp functions are such devices. The axis must be parallel to the road bearing plane, with ±3° in each direction.

Paragraph 5.3 requires the axis to be parallel to the median longitudinal plane for all signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps. The rear lamp falls in the 'all other' case. The ±3° tolerance is preserved.

The last sentence of 5.3 requires compliance with the manufacturer's specific fitting instructions. The cited quote is the tolerance wording, but the obligation is in the same clause and applies to the lamp.

Paragraph 5.4 sets the verification condition for lamp height and orientation: vehicle unladen on a flat horizontal surface, AFS neutral. It applies to lamps fitted to an M1 vehicle when there are no specific instructions.

Paragraph 5.5.1 applies to lamps constituting a pair, under the 5.5 lead-in 'in the absence of specific instructions'. The spec does not say the lamp is fitted as a pair. A rear lamp on a passenger car is normally one of a left/right pair, so it is applicable.

Paragraph 5.5.2 requires paired lamps to be symmetrical to one another, except for interior structure. The exception is preserved. A left/right rear lamp pair on an M1 is the usual case, though the spec does not state it.
Paragraph 5.5.3 requires paired lamps to satisfy the same colorimetric requirements. It applies to the rear lamp as one of a pair, and the lens defines its colour.
Paragraph 5.5.4 requires paired lamps to have substantially identical photometric characteristics. The matched-pair exception is preserved. It applies to the rear lamp as one of a pair.
Paragraph 5.7.1 permits grouping, combining or reciprocal incorporation only if all requirements are fulfilled. The spec describes a single housing combining several light functions, so it applies.

Paragraph 5.7.1.1 applies because the housing groups several functions. Photometric and colorimetric requirements are met with the other functions OFF. The exception for a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with other functions is preserved.
Clause 6.4.2.1 requires one reversing lamp and allows a second on M1 vehicles. The spec says the product is for an M1 passenger car and includes a reversing lamp.
Clause 6.4.2.3 requires reversing devices to be type-approved to UN R23 or UN R148 (00 or later series). The product includes a reversing lamp function.
Clause 6.4.4.2 sets the mounting height at 250 mm to 1,200 mm. The 1,400 mm limit is correctly restricted to off-road N2G, N3G, M2G and M3G vehicles, which do not include this M1 product.

Clause 6.4.4.3 requires the reversing lamp at the rear of the vehicle. The side-mounting exception covers only the optional devices on vehicles over 6,000 mm, so it does not apply to M1. Omitting it is acceptable.
Clause 6.4.5.1 gives the angles α = 15° up and 5° down. β is 45° each way for one device, or 45° outwards and 30° inwards for two. This matches the candidate for a rear-installed reversing lamp.

Clause 6.7.1 says S1/S2 stop lamps are mandatory on all vehicle categories. It also says S3/S4 devices are mandatory on M1 and N1, except chassis-cabs and N1 vehicles with open cargo space. The product is an M1 rear lamp with a stop lamp function, and the candidate keeps the clause's conditions and exceptions. The spec doesn't give the stop lamp's S-category, but the clause covers all of them.

Clause 6.7.2 requires two S1/S2 devices and one S3/S4 device. They must be type-approved to UN R7 (02 or later series) or UN R148 (00 or later series). The product's stop lamp contributes to the required stop lamps on an M1 vehicle, and the candidate keeps the number and approval conditions. The spec doesn't say which S-category the lamp is or what approval it holds, so those details can't be checked.

UN R48 applies to M and N vehicles, and the product is an M1 rear lamp with a stop lamp function. Paragraph 6.7.7.1 requires all stop lamps to switch ON together on the braking signal defined in UN R13 and R13-H. The candidate keeps that wording. The exception in 6.7.7.2 is a separate clause, so leaving it out does not change the obligation. The word "wired" in the candidate's reason is a mild gloss.

Paragraph 6.7.8 sits under the stop lamp requirements, and the product has a stop lamp. The candidate keeps the source's conditions: a tell-tale is optional, and a failure tell-tale is mandatory only if the component regulation requires it. The spec does not say whether the component regulation requires one, but the candidate does not assume it does.
Clause 6.10.1 makes rear position lamps (R, R1, R2) mandatory. The product is an M1 rear lamp with a rear position lamp function, and UN R48 applies to M and N vehicles.

Clause 6.10.2 requires two rear position lamps approved to UN R7 (02 or later series) or UN R148 (00 or later series). The candidate wording matches this, and the product includes a rear position lamp.
Clause 6.10.4.1 sets the 400 mm outer-edge limit. It excludes optional rear lamps and sets no special inner-edge distance for M1 vehicles. The candidate keeps these conditions, and the product is M1.

Clause 6.10.4.2 sets a mounting height of 350 to 1,500 mm. The 2,100 mm exception applies only if the bodywork makes 1,500 mm impossible and no optional lamps are installed. The candidate keeps these limits, and the product has a rear position lamp.
Clause 6.10.4.3 requires the rear position lamp to be positioned at the rear of the vehicle. This applies to the product's rear position function.

Clause 6.7.4.1 sets the 400 mm outer-edge limit for S1/S2 devices on M1/N1 vehicles. The product is an M1 rear lamp with a stop lamp, which is a side-mounted S1/S2 device. The candidate keeps the condition and limit.

Clause 6.7.4.2.1 sets the 350–1500 mm height range for S1/S2 devices, with the 2100 mm exception when bodywork prevents 1500 mm and optional lamps are not installed. The product's stop lamp function falls under this. The candidate keeps the limits and the exception.
Clause 6.7.4.4 requires S1/S2 devices to be at the rear of the vehicle. The product is a rear lamp with a stop lamp function.

Clause 6.7.5 sets horizontal visibility of 45° left and right for S1/S2 devices. It allows the inward angle to be reduced to 20° under the H plane for stop lamps mounted below 750 mm. The candidate preserves this.

Clause 6.7.5 sets vertical visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal for S1/S2 devices. It allows the downward angle to be reduced to 5° below 750 mm and the upward angle to be reduced to 5° for optional lamps above 2100 mm. The candidate preserves these exceptions.
Clause 6.7.6 requires the stop lamp to be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle. The product is a rear lamp with a stop function.
UN R48 6.14.1 makes a non-triangular rear retro-reflector mandatory on motor vehicles. The product is an M1 rear lamp module that includes a retro-reflector.

UN R48 6.14.2 requires two retro-reflectors approved as Class IA or IB under UN R3 (02 series or later) or UN R150 (00 series or later). It also permits additional devices that do not impair the mandatory ones. The candidate keeps these conditions, and the product includes a retro-reflector.

UN R48 6.14.4.1 sets a 400 mm maximum from the vehicle's extreme outer edge and no special inner-edge distance requirement for M1. The candidate reflects both, and the product is an M1 rear lamp with a retro-reflector.

UN R48 6.14.4.2 sets a height of 250–900 mm, rising to 1,200 mm if grouped with a rear lamp and 1,500 mm if the bodywork shape makes the lower limits impossible. The candidate keeps these limits, and the spec shows the retro-reflector grouped with the rear lamps in one housing.

Clause 6.14.4.3 is in the section on non-triangular rear retro-reflectors. The product is an M1 rear lamp with an integrated prism retro-reflector, and UN R48 covers M and N categories. The obligation (position at the rear of the vehicle) matches the clause. The spec doesn't state the retro-reflector's shape. Triangular ones are prohibited on motor vehicles (6.15.1), so non-triangular is the reasonable reading.

Clause 6.14.5 sets visibility angles of 30° inwards and outwards and 10° above and below horizontal. The downward angle may be reduced to 5° below 750 mm. The candidate keeps all of these limits and the exception. The clause applies to the product's non-triangular retro-reflector once installed.
Clause 6.14.6 says the orientation is rearwards. The product's retro-reflector is part of a rear lamp, so the clause applies and the candidate restates it accurately.

Clause 6.14.7 allows the retro-reflector's illuminating surface to share parts with the apparent surface of another rear lamp. The product combines several lamp functions and a retro-reflector in one housing. The candidate correctly describes this as a permission and not a mandatory requirement.

Paragraph 6.19.7.5 of UN R48 says the rear position lamps shall be ON when daytime running lamps (DRLs) are ON. They may be OFF, and stay OFF, while ambient light is above 7,000 lux (Annex 13). R48 scope covers M and N vehicles, and the product is an M1 rear lamp with a rear position lamp function. The candidate keeps the condition and the lux exception. Its "only while" wording is a slightly stronger reading of the source's "as long as", but it matches the meaning. It leaves out the optional "other lamps" of paragraph 5.11, which does not change the obligation. The spec does not say the vehicle has DRLs. The rule is conditional ("when DRLs are ON"), and it applies to the vehicle's electrical connection of the rear position lamp, so the match holds.

R48 applies to M and N vehicles. 6.23.1 makes the emergency stop signal mandatory on motor vehicles, and it says the signal is given by all stop or direction-indicator lamps operating together. The M1 rear lamp contains the stop lamp, so that lamp is one of those operated. The candidate leaves out the conditions in 6.23.7 (4 Hz flashing, automatic on/off, speed above 50 km/h). It does not contradict them. The obligation is placed on the vehicle, so the lamp's part in it is an inference. The spec does not say the stop lamp can flash.

results.reason: Annex 1 / 9.4 is a yes/no field in the UN R48 communication for a vehicle type, about installing lighting devices. The product is a rear lamp module, not a vehicle, and the spec gives no vehicle-level approval. The clause creates no requirement on the lamp. Having a reversing lamp does not turn this form field into a product obligation.

Annex 1 / 9.9 is a yes/no field in the vehicle-type installation communication under UN R48. The product is a lamp component, not a vehicle. The clause sets no obligation on the lamp, so the stop lamp match is based only on a shared keyword.

Annex 1 / 9.12 is a yes/no field in the vehicle-type installation communication under UN R48. The product is a rear lamp module, not a vehicle. The clause sets no requirement on the lamp, so the rear position lamp match is based only on a shared keyword.

Clause 6.10.5.1 sets the geometric visibility angles for the rear position lamp, and the product has one. The candidate keeps the 750 mm and 2,100 mm reduction conditions. The M1 alternative in 6.10.5.2 is an optional alternative, so it does not contradict this obligation.
Clause 6.10.6 requires the rear position lamp to be oriented rearwards, and the product has a rear position lamp.

Clause 6.10.7 requires electrical connections in accordance with 5.11. The candidate keeps the direction-indicator exception as conditional on reciprocal incorporation, which the product does not have.

Clause 6.10.8 requires a closed-circuit tell-tale for the rear position lamp, combined with the front position lamps' tell-tale. The candidate keeps the daytime running lamp exception and the failure tell-tale condition. The tell-tale is a vehicle-level installation item, not part of the lamp module, so confidence is lower.

Annex 1 item 9.12.1 asks for a yes/no declaration on a failure tell-tale for rear position lamps. It sits under 9.12, and the product has a rear position lamp. The spec does not say whether a tell-tale is fitted, but the obligation is only to declare yes or no, so that gap does not matter. The scope covers M1 vehicles.

Annex 1 item 9.16 asks for a yes/no declaration on non-triangular rear retro-reflectors. The product includes a retro-reflector and is an M1 vehicle rear lamp, which is within R48 scope. The spec does not state the reflector shape. Triangular rear retro-reflectors are normally for trailers, so non-triangular is the right form item for M1. That last point comes from my knowledge of R48, not from a clause I read here. The candidate keeps the yes/no wording.

UN R7 applies to rear position lamps and stop lamps for M1 vehicles, and the product has both. Para 2.1 says the application must be submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark or by their duly accredited representative. The candidate keeps that meaning.

Para 2.1.1 requires the application to specify the purpose(s) of the device and whether it may be used in an assembly of two lamps of the same kind/type. The product combines rear position and stop lamps, so R7 applies. The candidate preserves the clause's wording.

UN R48 applies to M and N vehicles for installation of lighting and signalling devices. Annex 9 §1.1 requires checking lamp position in width, height and length against the cited general paragraphs and each lamp's individual specifications. The product is an M1 rear lamp with position, stop and reversing lamps, so this applies. The candidate wording keeps the clause's conditions. Confidence is moderate because the product is a lamp module and the clause is a vehicle-level conformity-of-production check.

Annex 9 §1.2.1 requires geometric visibility angles to be checked per §2.10.7 against each lamp's individual specifications. It allows the angle limits an allowance for the ±3° mounting variation in §5.3. This applies to the M1 rear lamp's signalling functions. The candidate keeps the allowance as optional ("may"), as the source does. Confidence is moderate because the check is made at vehicle level.

The product is an M1 rear lamp module with a red lens, so UN R48 applies. Paragraph 5.10.1 says red light from a rear lamp must not be visible from the front. Paragraph 5.10.4.1 uses Annex 4 Zone 1 for the check. Annex 4 sets that zone at 1 m to 2.2 m above the ground, with vertical planes at 15° outwards from the median longitudinal plane. The candidate leaves out the overall-width contact-point detail and the 25 m observation distance in 5.10.4.1, but it does not contradict them. The product spec does not say the lamp is fitted on the vehicle rear, only that it is a rear lamp, so this is a vehicle-installation check on the lamp.

results.reason: Annex 9 / 1.6 requires the presence, number, colour, arrangement and category of lamps to be checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings. The lamps must also meet paragraphs 5.15 and 5.16 and the individual lamp specifications. The candidate keeps all of these elements. The product is an M1 rear lamp module with position, stop and reversing functions, so these are lamps within R48's scope (categories M and N). Two weaknesses: this is a vehicle-level conformity-of-production check, and the spec does not mention lamp markings. Naming the rear position, stop and reversing functions is only an illustration, not a new obligation.

The product is an M1 rear lamp with rear position and stop lamp functions, which UN R7 covers. Paragraph 5.2 requires the devices to operate satisfactorily in normal use despite vibration and to keep the prescribed characteristics. The candidate states this without adding or dropping any condition. I did not search R7's scope clause. This rests on the product spec and the cited clause text.

The product has a rear position lamp and a stop lamp, and UN R7 covers both. Paragraph 2.1.4 requires the application to state whether the intensity is steady or variable. The candidate keeps the category lists as the clause gives them.

Paragraph 2.2.1 requires drawings in triplicate for each device type. This applies to the R7 position and stop lamp functions in the product. The candidate keeps the listed contents of the drawings. Its "any interdependent lamp combination" wording is close enough to the clause's "in the case of an interdependent lamp system".

Paragraph 2.2.2 requires a technical description that gives the LED light source category (UN R128) or the light source module code. It excepts lamps with non-replaceable light sources, and the candidate keeps that exception. The product uses LED modules. The spec does not say whether they are replaceable, but the exception is preserved either way.

Paragraph 2.2.4 requires two samples. It allows two identical samples for one side when the left and right devices are symmetrical. The candidate states this correctly. The product's position and stop lamp functions come under R7, so it applies. Leaving out the variable-intensity control sentence is fine because it only applies to variable-intensity lamps.

Clause 4.2.2.2 requires the letter "R" on rear position lamp devices. It is followed or not by "1" for steady intensity or "2" for variable intensity. The product has a rear position lamp function, and the candidate keeps the clause's conditions.

Clause 4.2.2.5 requires "S" followed by 1, 2, 3 or 4 on stop-lamp devices. The figure depends on steady or variable intensity and on the S3 or S4 requirements. The product includes a stop lamp, and the candidate summarises the clause accurately.

Clause 4.2.2.6 covers devices that combine a rear position lamp and a stop-lamp. These carry "R", "R1" or "R2" and "S1" or "S2", separated by a horizontal dash. The product combines both lamps in one housing, so the clause applies.

The clause is an Annex 9 conformity-of-production check at vehicle level. It covers red light visible to the front and white light visible to the rear. The spec describes a red rear lamp module with a white reversing lamp, but it gives no information on how visibility is limited once the lamp is mounted on the vehicle. The cited product evidence, 'Reversing illumination', does not establish that this check applies to the lamp itself.

Annex 9 1.4 requires the electrical connections to be checked by switching on every lamp supplied by the vehicle's electrical system. The rear lamp is an electrically powered M1 lighting module (LEDs on a PCB), so the check applies to its lamp functions once it is fitted to the vehicle. The candidate wording matches the clause. It is a vehicle-level conformity check rather than a lamp-specific requirement, which is why confidence is only moderate.

The second sentence of Annex 9 1.4 requires lamps and tell-tales to function in accordance with paragraphs 5.11 to 5.14 and with each lamp's individual specifications. The product's stop lamp, position lamp and reversing lamp are lamps within that scope. The candidate wording preserves the clause. Confidence is moderate because this is a vehicle-level conformity check.

6.23.2 only cross-refers to 6.5.2 or 6.7.2. It is a vehicle-level installation rule for the emergency stop signal. The spec lists a stop lamp but never says the rear lamp provides an emergency stop signal. The candidate's reason assumes this, so the product facts are missing.
6.23.3 only cross-refers to 6.5.3 or 6.7.3. It is a vehicle installation rule, and the spec does not state an emergency stop signal function for the lamp. Applicability is not established.
6.23.4 only cross-refers to 6.5.4 or 6.7.4. It is a vehicle installation rule, and the spec does not state an emergency stop signal function for the lamp. Applicability is not established.
6.23.5 only cross-refers to 6.5.5 or 6.7.5. It is a vehicle installation rule, and the spec does not state an emergency stop signal function for the lamp. Applicability is not established.
6.23.6 only cross-refers to 6.5.6 or 6.7.6. It is a vehicle installation rule, and the spec does not state an emergency stop signal function for the lamp. Applicability is not established.

6.23.7.1 covers the electrical connections of the vehicle's emergency stop signal. The spec says only that the rear lamp has a stop lamp and LED sources. It does not say the lamp flashes or is wired into an emergency stop signal. Flashing at 4 Hz is therefore not confirmed as a product-level obligation.

6.23.7.2 is a vehicle electrical-connection requirement. The spec gives no evidence that the rear lamp's stop lamp takes part in an emergency stop signal. Being part of the rear lamp does not establish that.
Automatic ON/OFF switching is vehicle control logic under 6.23.7.3. The spec gives no evidence that the rear lamp provides or is controlled as an emergency stop signal.

The 50 km/h speed condition and the emergency braking logic signal are vehicle and braking-system conditions. The spec has no evidence that the rear lamp implements or is subject to this. The text preserves the clause, but applicability to the lamp module is not shown.

Switch-off on loss of the emergency braking signal or hazard warning activation is vehicle-level logic. The spec has no evidence that the rear lamp implements it or is subject to it. The text preserves the clause, but applicability is not shown.

Paragraph 3.1 applies to devices submitted for approval. The rear lamp combines rear position and stop lamp functions, which UN R7 covers. The trade name or mark requirement and its legible, indelible condition are preserved.
Paragraph 3.3 applies to the lamp submitted for approval, and the candidate keeps the requirement for a space shown in the drawings. The product includes R7 lamp functions (rear position and stop).

Paragraph 3.6.1 applies only to lamps with light source modules. The spec says only 'LED modules on PCB'. It does not say whether these are light source modules in the regulatory sense (a defined optical part with its own identification). The obligation text is otherwise accurate.

Paragraph 3.6.2 applies only where the lamp has light source modules. The spec does not establish that the 'LED modules on PCB' are regulatory light source modules. The candidate's wording on the MD code is consistent with the clause.

Paragraph 3.6.3 applies only where the lamp has light source modules. The spec does not establish that the 'LED modules on PCB' are regulatory light source modules. The obligation text matches the clause.

Paragraph 4.1.1 refers to the two samples submitted under 2.2.4. The product spec does not describe an interdependent lamp system, so the same-applicant sentence has no product evidence. The candidate also restates "approval shall be granted" as "granted only if", which the source does not say.

The product combines position, stop and reversing functions in one housing, so this is a grouped or combined unit. Paragraph 4.1.2 requires each lamp in such a unit to satisfy R7 or another Regulation. The headlamp exception is irrelevant here.

The product has rear position and stop lamp functions, which R7 covers. Paragraph 4.1.3 assigns an approval number to each approved type. The candidate correctly states the amendment-series digits and the colour-extension exception.
